definition_zh: 训练；培训；锻炼；（动物）驯养
definition_en: the process of teaching or being taught the skills needed for a job, sport, or activity
core_image: 操场上反复跑动的身影，一天接一天
scene: 天还没亮，跑道上已经有几个人在跑第四圈，呼吸白得像雾。 She is in training for the marathon and runs every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 training 是「训练」（第 1 个义项：为掌握技能或备战而反复练习的过程）；句意为她正在为马拉松训练，每天早上都跑。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「训练」；也指名次「火车」
由 train 加 -ee 构成，义为「受训者」
由 train 加 -er 构成，义为「教练」

senses.title: The process of learning a job
senses.definition: the teaching and practice that prepares someone for a job or task
senses.definitionCN: 为某份工作或任务做准备的教学与练习
senses.example: New staff get two weeks of training before they start.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工上岗前要接受两周培训。
senses.why: The -ing form names the activity of the verb train, and this is its most general sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个 -ing 形式指动词 train 的活动本身，这是它最一般的义项。

senses.title: Regular exercise for a sport
senses.definition: the regular exercise and practice an athlete does to prepare for competition
senses.definitionCN: 运动员为备战比赛而做的定期锻炼与练习
senses.example: Her training includes swimming twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的训练包括每周游泳两次。
senses.why: Sport makes the forming of skill visible, day after day, and this sense is now the most familiar.
senses.whyCN: 体育让技能的塑造日复一日地可见，这一义项如今最为人所熟悉。

senses.title: The teaching of an animal
senses.definition: the work of teaching an animal to obey and perform tasks
senses.definitionCN: 教动物服从并执行任务的工作
senses.example: Dog training takes patience and a great many small rewards.
senses.exampleCN: 驯狗需要耐心和许多小小的奖励。
senses.why: Animals as well as people can be brought along a course of practice, so the same noun covers them.
senses.whyCN: 动物同人一样能被带着走完练习课程，所以同一个名词也覆盖它们。

senses.title: A state of being prepared
senses.definition: the condition of being fit and ready, especially in the phrase in training
senses.definitionCN: 处于体能与准备就绪的状态，尤见于 in training
senses.example: The whole team is in training for the spring games.
senses.exampleCN: 全队都在为春季运动会训练。
senses.why: The activity becomes a state one can be in, so the noun describes readiness rather than the exercises.
senses.whyCN: 这种活动变成可以置身其中一种状态，于是名词描述的是准备程度而非练习本身。

senses.title: Education for a profession
senses.definition: the formal preparation for a profession such as teaching or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 为教师、医生等职业所做的正规准备
senses.example: Teacher training now includes a full year in school.
senses.exampleCN: 如今的师资培训包含一整年的在校实践。
senses.why: Long professional preparation is named by the same word because it is the same practice over a longer course.
senses.whyCN: 长期的专业准备用同一个词，因为它只是把同样的练习拉到了更长的课程上。

intro.en: Training is the noun from the verb train, whose French source trahiner, to drag, goes back to Latin trahere, to pull.
intro.cn: training 是由动词 train 派生的名词，train 来自古法语 trahiner（拖），其源头是拉丁语 trahere（拉）。

items.en: Trahere means to pull or draw, and its participle tractus underlies many English words.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 意为拉、拖，其分词 tractus 支撑许多英语词。

items.en: Trahiner means to drag along, and from it English takes the verb train.
items.cn: 古法语 trahiner 意为沿地拖，英语的动词 train 由此而来。

items.en: By the sixteenth century to train means to lead a person by practice into a skill.
items.cn: 十六世纪时 to train 已意为通过练习把人带入某项技能。

items.en: The noun training spreads with armies, schools, and later with organised sport in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 training 随军队、学校以及十九世纪有组织的体育运动而传播。

items.en: Job training and on-the-job training become fixed phrases of industry in the twentieth century.
items.cn: job training 与 on-the-job training 在二十世纪成为工业界的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the train family, while the near-meaning group gathers words for teaching, practice, and preparation.
note.cn: 形近组收集 train 词族，近义组收集表示教学、练习与准备的词。

entries.definition: to teach a skill by practice
a person receiving training
a person who gives training
the activity of buying and selling
entries.definitionCN: 交易，拼写相近而来源不同

entries.definition: the broad process of teaching and learning
repeated exercise to gain skill
the training given by a coach

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the -ing formation, from the fixed phrases with receive and in, and from the picture of the early track.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从 -ing 构词、receive training 与 in training 固定搭配以及清晨跑道画面入手。

normal.en: Train plus -ing: the -ing turns the verb of teaching into the whole activity and its sessions.
normal.cn: train 加 -ing，这个后缀把「教」的动词变成整个活动及其课程。

normal.en: In training is a state; training course is a thing you attend.
normal.cn: in training 是一种状态，training course 是你要去上的课。

normal.en: A trainee is acted upon, a trainer acts, and training is the action between them.
normal.cn: 受训者被施加，教练施加，而 training 是两者之间的行动。

normal.en: Training as a noun is uncountable: say two weeks of training, not two trainings.
normal.cn: 作为名词不可数：说 two weeks of training，不说 two trainings。

normal.en: Every skill is a line of practice followed until it becomes easy.
normal.cn: 每项技能都是一条练习出来的线，走到它变容易为止。

abstract.en: Picture a white line on a track, passed over again and again before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道上的白线，在日出前被一次又一次越过。

abstract.en: Think of a whistle sounding, then the same movement repeated exactly.
abstract.cn: 想哨声一响，同一个动作被一模一样地重复。

abstract.en: Training is patience turned into habit.
abstract.cn: 训练是被养成习惯的耐心。

examples.en: All drivers here receive two days of safety training.
examples.cn: 这里所有司机都要接受两天安全培训。

examples.en: He is in training for the hill race.
examples.cn: 他正在为山地赛跑训练。

examples.en: The training of young horses takes years.
examples.cn: 驯养年轻马匹要花好几年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹宁」——教练一吹哨，宁可累也要再来一遍，这就是训练。

root: 拉丁语 trahere（拉、拖）→ 古法语 trahiner（拖）→ 英语动词 train（培养）→ train + -ing → training。词族有 trainee、trainer。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins with the general activity of forming skill, narrows to sport and to animals, rises into a state of readiness, and widens again into formal professional education.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词先指塑造技能的一般活动，收窄到体育与动物，上升为准备就绪的状态，再扩展为正规的专业教育。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one movement repeated until it becomes easy.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个动作被重复到变容易为止。

branches.en: The general work preparation.
branches.cn: 一般的工作准备。

branches.en: The athlete's daily exercise.
branches.cn: 运动员的日常锻炼。

branches.en: The teaching of animals.
branches.cn: 对动物的驯养。

branches.en: The state of being ready.
branches.cn: 准备就绪的状态。

branches.en: The long formal preparation for a profession.
branches.cn: 职业所需的长期正规准备。

intro.en: Training is the verb train with the English -ing suffix, and its family adds -ee and -er to the same verb.
intro.cn: training 是动词 train 加英语 -ing 后缀，其词族在同一动词上加 -ee 与 -er。

latinIntro.cn: 下面列出这一词族背后的拉丁「拉」动词及其分词。

items.exampleCN: 这个词干以 train 的形式进入英语。

items.example: Training is the activity of the verb.
items.exampleCN: training 是动词的活动形式。

items.example: A trainee is trained by a trainer.

items.exampleCN: job training 为新员工做准备。

items.example: A training course runs for weeks.
On-the-job training happens at the bench.

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；可怕的
definition_en: feeling afraid, worried about something, or causing great fear
core_image: 小狗听到鞭炮声，夹着尾巴钻进桌底，只露出一双发抖的眼睛
scene: 小狗听到鞭炮声，夹着尾巴躲到桌底。 The fearful dog hid under the table.
sceneCN: 这里 fearful 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：害怕的小狗躲在桌子下面。

senses.title: Feeling afraid
senses.definition: feeling afraid of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物感到害怕
senses.example: The fearful child refused to enter the dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 害怕的孩子不肯进入黑暗的房间。
senses.why: This is the central sense describing a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: 这是形容人或动物的核心义。

senses.title: Worried
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 担心坏事可能发生
senses.example: She was fearful about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心结果。
senses.why: Fear also appears as milder anxiety.
senses.whyCN: fear 也可表现为较轻的焦虑。

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: very bad or frightening in appearance or effect
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或后果上极为可怕
senses.example: A fearful storm struck the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一场可怕的风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: The suffix -ful can mean full of or inspiring the root.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 既可表示充满，也可表示引起某种感受。

intro.en: Fearful was formed in English from fear with the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fearful 由 fear 在英语中加后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: The root named sudden danger.
items.cn: 该词根表示突发的危险。

items.en: Fǣr meant peril or calamity.
items.cn: fǣr 意为危险或灾祸。

items.en: Fere came to mean the emotion of fright.
items.cn: fere 开始表示惊恐的情绪。

items.en: Fearful appeared meaning full of fear.
items.cn: fearful 出现，意为充满恐惧的。

items.en: The word also describes things that cause fear.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也形容引起恐惧的事物。

note.en: Fearful is compared with similar-looking words and with words for being afraid.
note.cn: 把 fearful 与形近词以及表示害怕的词作比较。

causing fear
without fear
feeling fear
made afraid

normalIntro.en: Fearful means full of fear, worried, or frightening to others.
normalIntro.cn: fearful 意为充满恐惧、担心，或令他人害怕。

normal.en: Fearful of means afraid of something.
normal.cn: fearful of 意为害怕某事物。

normal.en: Fearful about shows worry rather than terror.
normal.cn: fearful about 更多表示担忧而非极度恐惧。

normal.en: A fearful storm is a frightening storm.
normal.cn: a fearful storm 指可怕的风暴。

normal.en: Fearful and fearless are opposites built on fear.
normal.cn: fearful 与 fearless 是以 fear 为基础的反义词。

normal.en: Fearfully can describe both fear and awe.
normal.cn: fearfully 既可形容恐惧，也可形容敬畏。

abstract.en: A person can be fearful, and a storm can be fearful too.
abstract.cn: 人可以害怕，风暴也可以令人害怕。

abstract.en: The same suffix makes both full of and causing.
abstract.cn: 同一个后缀既能表示「充满」，也能表示「引起」。

abstract.en: Fearful attention can sharpen the senses.
abstract.cn: 带有恐惧的注意力会让感官更敏锐。

examples.en: The fearful child refused to enter the dark room.
examples.cn: 害怕的孩子不肯进入黑暗的房间。

examples.en: She was fearful about the results.

examples.en: A fearful storm struck the coast.
examples.cn: 一场可怕的风暴袭击了海岸。

root: 由 fear（恐惧）加后缀 -ful 构成，核心义「充满恐惧的；引起恐惧的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fearful means feeling afraid, worried about something, or frightening enough to cause fear.
sensesIntro.cn: fearful 意为感到害怕、对某事担心，或可怕到引起恐惧。

core.en: Full of fear, or frightening enough to produce it.
core.cn: 充满恐惧，或可怕到足以引起恐惧。

branches.en: A person or animal that feels afraid.
branches.cn: 感到害怕的人或动物。

branches.en: A mind uneasy about what may happen.
branches.cn: 对可能发生之事感到不安的心。

branches.en: Something so bad that it frightens others.
branches.cn: 糟糕到令他人害怕的事物。

branches.en: The frightened and the frightening face each other.
branches.cn: 害怕者与可怕者彼此相对。

branches.en: Fear of the present and worry about the future blend together.
branches.cn: 对当下的恐惧与对未来的担忧交织在一起。

intro.en: Fearful forms words for fear, bravery, and the state of being afraid.
intro.cn: fearful 构成表示恐惧、勇敢与胆怯状态的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: She glanced fearfully at the door.
items.exampleCN: 她害怕地瞥了一眼门口。

items.example: His fearfulness showed in his voice.
items.exampleCN: 他的胆怯从声音里流露出来。

items.example: The fearless rider calmed the horse.
They walked fearlessly into the fog.

items.exampleCN: 她的无畏鼓舞了整个小组。

items.example: The fearsome noise echoed in the hall.
items.exampleCN: 可怕的响声在大厅里回荡。
令人害怕的风暴始终没有到来。

definition_zh: 学院；专科学校；研究院；学会
definition_en: a school for special training, or a society of scholars and artists
core_image: 石砌大门上刻着院徽，学生抱着乐谱走进去
scene: 街角那栋老楼门口挂着铜牌，里面传出练琴的声音。 She trained at the national academy for three years.
sceneCN: 这里的 academy 指「专科学校」（第 1 个义项：专门培养某种技能的学校）；句意是她在国家级的学院受训三年。

pos.zh: 学院；专科学校；研究院；学会

senses.title: A training school
senses.definition: a school that trains people in a special skill
senses.definitionCN: 专门培养某种技能的学校
senses.example: He studied at a music academy.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所音乐学院学习。
senses.why: A grove of study became a place of specialised teaching, and that is the first modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 治学的园子成了专门授课之处，这是第一个现代义项。

senses.title: A society of scholars
senses.definition: an honoured body of scholars or artists
senses.definitionCN: 由学者或艺术家组成的荣誉团体
senses.example: The academy elects ten new members a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该学会每年遴选十名新成员。
senses.why: Plato's group was a company of thinkers, and later societies kept the word.
senses.whyCN: 柏拉图的团体是一群思想者，后来的学会沿用了这个词。

senses.title: A military school
senses.definition: a college that trains officers
senses.definitionCN: 培养军官的高等学校
senses.example: He entered the military academy at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十八岁进入军事学院。
senses.why: An officer's training is a special skill, so the word fits military schools.
senses.whyCN: 军官训练也是一种专门技能，因此这个词也适用于军校。

senses.title: A school of art
senses.definition: a college for painting, music or drama
senses.definitionCN: 教授绘画、音乐或戏剧的院校
senses.example: The academy holds a show every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这所艺术院校每年春天举办展览。
senses.why: Art too is taught in a special school, and the word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 艺术也在专门的学校里教授，这个词自然涵盖它。

senses.title: A film prize
senses.definition: in academy award, the prize given by a film academy
senses.definitionCN: 在 academy award 中，指由电影学院颁发的奖项
senses.example: She won an academy award for the film.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭这部影片赢得了学院奖。
senses.why: A body of film makers is an academy, and its prize took the name.
senses.whyCN: 电影从业者的团体就是一个学院，它的奖项便沿用了这个名字。

senses.title: A secondary school
senses.definition: in Scotland and the United States, a school for older pupils
senses.definitionCN: 在苏格兰与美国，指招收较大学生的中学
senses.example: The academy in our town takes pupils from twelve to eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 我们镇上的中学招收十二到十八岁的学生。
senses.why: Older schools kept the old name after they became local secondary schools.
senses.whyCN: 一些老学校在变成地方中学后，仍保留了这个旧名。

senses.title: Plato's school
senses.definition: the school of philosophy founded by Plato
senses.definitionCN: 柏拉图创立的哲学学派
senses.example: The academy lasted for centuries after Plato.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图之后，这所学园延续了数百年。
senses.why: The original academy is the historical source of every later sense.
senses.whyCN: 最初的学园是所有后世义项的历史源头。

senses.title: A private learned body
senses.definition: a private society that promotes an art or science
senses.definitionCN: 推动某门艺术或科学的私人团体
senses.example: The academy publishes its own journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学术团体出版自己的期刊。
senses.why: Societies that fund and publish research borrow the dignified old name.
senses.whyCN: 资助并出版研究的团体，借用了这个庄重的旧名。

intro.en: The word is the name of the grove near Athens where Plato taught.
intro.cn: 这个词是雅典附近柏拉图授课那片园子的名字。

items.en: Akademeia was a grove near Athens named for a hero.
items.cn: Akademeia 是雅典附近以一位英雄命名的园子。

items.en: Plato taught there, and the place gave its name to his school.
items.cn: 柏拉图在此授课，这地方便成了他学派的名称。

items.en: academia named a place of higher learning.

items.en: it now names schools of special training and film prizes.

note.cn: 形近组是 academic 词族；近义组是别的表示学校与学术团体的名称。

abstract.cn: 想象一道老石门上方的铜牌。

abstract.en: Picture a hall where every chair faces a single board.
abstract.cn: 想象一间大厅，所有椅子都朝向一块黑板。

abstract.en: Think of a score left open on a music stand.
abstract.cn: 想象谱架上摊开的乐谱。

examples.cn: 她凭这部影片获得了学院奖。

sensesIntro.en: One grove of philosophy grows into training schools, learned societies, local schools and a film prize.
sensesIntro.cn: 一片哲学园子长成了专科学校、学术团体、地方中学与电影奖项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone gate with a bronze plaque.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂着铜牌的石门。

branches.en: the training school and its original grove
branches.cn: 培训学校与它最初的园子

branches.en: public and private learned bodies
branches.cn: 公开与私人的学术团体

branches.en: the military college
branches.cn: 军事学院

branches.en: the school of art
branches.cn: 艺术院校

branches.en: the film prize and the local secondary school
branches.cn: 电影奖项与地方中学

intro.en: The word is a Greek place name that became a general noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语地名变成了普通名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin academia kept the school's name alive through the Middle Ages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 让这所学园的名字在中世纪得以延续。

definition_zh: 机修工；技工；力学；机械师
definition_en: a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines, especially car engines; also a skilled worker who builds or operates machinery, and the science of motion treated as one subject
core_image: 一个人俯身钻进车底，手上沾满机油，用扳手拧紧一颗松动的螺丝
scene: 修理厂的卷帘门半开着，一辆旧车被千斤顶顶起，车底的人影正举着灯查找漏油的地方。 The mechanic wiped his hands and told the owner the fault was only a loose screw.
sceneCN: 这里是「机修工」（第 1 个义项：修机器的人）；句意为机修工擦了擦手，告诉车主故障只是一颗松动的螺丝。图中可辨识物件：千斤顶、车底灯、扳手。

pos.zh: 机修工；技工；力学；机械师

derivatives.zh: 由 mechanic 加复数 -s 构成，指研究力与运动的「力学」
由 mechanic 加 -al 构成，义为「机械的；机械般的」
由 mechanical 加 -ly 构成，义为「机械地」
由同一希腊词干加 -ism 构成，义为「机械装置；机制」
由同一词干加 -ize 构成，义为「使机械化」

senses.title: A person who repairs machines
senses.definition: a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines, especially the engines of cars
senses.definitionCN: 以修理和保养机器为职业的人，尤指修汽车发动机的人
senses.example: The mechanic found the leak within ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工十分钟内就找到了漏点。
senses.why: Greek mekhane named a device or machine, and the ending that marks a person turned the idea of machinery into the craftsperson who keeps it running.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 mekhane 指装置、机械，加上表示「从事某事的人」的词尾，就把「机械」变成了让它保持运转的手艺人。

senses.title: The science of motion and forces
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies how forces move bodies, usually written as mechanics
senses.definitionCN: 研究力如何使物体运动的科学分支，通常写作 mechanics
senses.example: The old textbooks called the study of forces mechanic, a name now usually replaced by mechanics.
senses.exampleCN: 旧课本把研究力的学问称作 mechanic，如今通常改用 mechanics。
senses.why: The same Greek root named the machine and the knowledge of how it moves, so the science of forces kept the singular form in older English usage.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词根既指机械，也指关于它如何运动的知识，所以研究力的学问在较早的英语里保留了单数形式。

senses.title: A skilled worker who builds or operates machinery
senses.definition: a skilled manual worker who makes, fits or operates machinery, a sense common in older industrial English
senses.definitionCN: 制造、装配或操作机械的熟练手工劳动者，这一义项在较早的工业英语中常见
senses.example: The factory hired a mechanic who could set up the new lathe.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂雇了一名会给新机床做调试的机械师。
senses.why: Before motor cars, mekhane covered any machine, so a mechanic was simply the person who understood and handled machinery of any kind.
senses.whyCN: 在汽车出现之前，mekhane 泛指任何机械，因此 mechanic 就是懂机械、会摆弄机械的人，不限种类。

senses.title: Someone good at handling tools and devices
senses.definition: in informal use, a person who is unusually good at making things work or at handling tools and devices
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指特别擅长让东西运转、或摆弄工具与器械的人
senses.example: Ask him to fix the printer; he is a real mechanic with anything that has gears.
senses.exampleCN: 让他去修打印机吧，凡是带齿轮的东西他都很在行。
senses.why: Because a mechanic must diagnose a machine by feel and sound, the word widened from a job title to praise for anyone with that practical touch.
senses.whyCN: 机修工必须凭手感和声音判断机器毛病，于是这个词从职业名称扩展为对任何有这种实用本领之人的称赞。

intro.en: Mechanic is a Greek word about machines that travelled through Latin and French before English used it for the person, the craft and the science of motion.
intro.cn: mechanic 是希腊语中与机械有关的词，经拉丁语与法语传入英语，先指懂机械的人，也指这门手艺与运动之学。

items.en: Mekhane meant a device, a tool or a machine, and it also carried the idea of a trick or a contrivance.
items.cn: mekhane 意为装置、工具或机械，也带有「巧计、机关」的意思。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what belonged to machines and to inventing them, and it named the person who understood such things.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述属于机械、属于发明机械的事物，也用来称懂这类东西的人。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as mechanicus, an adjective and a noun for things and people concerned with machines.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词，作 mechanicus，既是形容词也作名词，指与机械有关的事物和人。

items.en: Old French used mecanique for the art of machines and for the science of motion, passing both senses toward English.
items.cn: 古法语用 mecanique 指机械技艺与运动之学，两种含义一起传向英语。

items.en: English kept mechanic for the person and mechanics for the science, while mechanical covers the adjective.
items.cn: 英语保留 mechanic 指人、mechanics 指力学，形容用法则由 mechanical 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Greek root for machines; the near-meaning group collects people who repair, design or operate them.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词根上的机械词族；近义组收修理、设计或操作机器的人。

entries.definition: Worked by machinery or done without thought, like a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 由机械驱动的；或像机器一样不加思考的。

entries.definition: The science of motion and forces, or the working parts of a machine.
entries.definitionCN: 研究运动与力的科学；也指机器的运转部件。

entries.definition: The parts that make a machine work, or a process by which something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器运转的部件；也指某事发生的机制。

entries.definition: To replace human or animal work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 用机器取代人力或畜力。

entries.definition: A person trained to do practical work with equipment or instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、会用设备或仪器做实际工作的人。

entries.definition: A person who designs, builds or maintains engines and structures.
entries.definitionCN: 设计、建造或维护发动机与工程结构的人。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to mend broken machines or equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 以修理坏掉的机器或设备为职业的人。

entries.definition: A person who operates a machine tool or makes machine parts.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机床或制作机器零件的人。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Greek noun for a machine; its family keeps returning to devices, their parts and the knowledge of how they move.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示机械的希腊名词上，同族词反复回到装置、部件以及关于它们如何运动的知识。

normal.en: Mekhane in Greek is a machine or a device, so a mechanic is the person attached to a machine.
normal.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 是机械、装置，所以 mechanic 就是与机械绑在一起的那个人。

normal.en: The same root gives mechanics, the science of how machines and bodies move.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 mechanics，即研究机器与物体如何运动的力学。

normal.en: Mechanical adds -al and means working like a machine, even without thought.
normal.cn: mechanical 加 -al，意为像机器一样运转，甚至不加思考。

normal.en: Mechanism is the inside of the machine, the parts that produce the motion.
normal.cn: mechanism 指机器内部那些产生运动的部件。

normal.en: Mechanize means to put a machine where a hand used to be.
normal.cn: mechanize 意为把原来用手的地方换成机器。

abstract.en: A mechanic knows a machine by sound before opening it, which shows how much of repair is attention.
abstract.cn: 机修工在拆开之前就能凭声音判断机器，这说明修理很大一部分靠的是留意。

abstract.en: From one Greek word for device grow the person, the science and the inner parts, three views of the same thing.
abstract.cn: 从一个表示装置的希腊词长出人、科学与内部构造，这是同一件事的三种看法。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that every working machine is held together by somebody who listens to it.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒人：每台能运转的机器背后，都有个在倾听它的人把它维持住。

examples.en: The mechanic traced the noise to a worn bearing.
examples.cn: 机修工把异响追查到一处磨损的轴承。

examples.en: Every mechanic in the shop knows that engine by sound.
examples.cn: 店里每个机修工都能凭声音认出那台发动机。

examples.en: A good mechanic listens before reaching for a wrench.
examples.cn: 好机修工先听，再伸手拿扳手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦卡尼克」——听起来像被麦子卡住的人，其实他正钻在车底修车；记住 mechanic 是机修工。

root: 希腊语 mekhane（机械、装置）经 mekhanikos 进入拉丁语 mechanicus，再经法语进入英语；同族词多与机械、运动与构造有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the machine and the person who keeps it working; from that come the science of motion, the older industrial craftsman and the informal praise for a practical hand.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是机械以及让它保持运转的人；由此分出运动之学、较早的工业技工，以及对有实用本领者的口语称赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person lying under a car, hands black with oil, tightening a loose screw.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人俯身钻在车底，双手沾满机油，正在拧紧一颗松动的螺丝。

branches.en: a garage light swinging under a raised car
branches.cn: 修车行里在顶起的车下晃动的灯

branches.en: a worker fitting a new part into an old frame
branches.cn: 工人把新部件装进旧机架

branches.en: a blackboard filled with arrows and forces
branches.cn: 写满箭头与力的黑板

branches.en: a neighbour who can coax any broken gadget back to life
branches.cn: 能把任何坏掉的小器具弄活的邻居

branches.en: an old workshop where apprentices learn by touch
branches.cn: 学徒靠手感学艺的老车间

intro.en: The word is carried by a Greek noun for a machine, its adjective, the Latin borrowings, and two English endings that mark a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示机械的希腊名词、它的形容词、拉丁语借词，以及两个标记「人」与「性质」的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 瘾；沉迷；依赖
definition_en: the condition of being unable to stop using something or doing something
core_image: 一个人反复伸手去拿同一只杯子，明知不该却停不下来
scene: 他花了一年才摆脱对止痛药的依赖。 It took him a year to beat his addiction to painkillers.
sceneCN: 这里的 addiction 是「瘾」（第 1 个义项：对某种物质无法自控的依赖）；句中指对止痛药的依赖。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀构成，义为「上瘾者」
加 -ed 构成，义为「上瘾的」

senses.title: Dependence on a substance
senses.definition: a strong need for a drug or drink that is very hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 对药物或酒类的强烈需求，极难戒断
senses.example: His addiction to painkillers began after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 他对止痛药的依赖始于那场车祸。
senses.why: Latin addictio meant handing someone over, and a person given over to a drug was later said to have an addiction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addictio 指把某人交付出去；当一个人被「交付」给某种药物，后来就说他有了 addiction。

senses.title: Being hooked on an activity
senses.definition: a strong habit of doing something that one cannot easily give up
senses.definitionCN: 难以轻易放弃的强烈习惯，对象是某项活动而非物质
senses.example: His addiction to video games worried his parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他对电子游戏的沉迷让父母担忧。
senses.why: As the word spread beyond drugs, the same loss of control was applied to games, work and shopping.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词走出药物范围，「失去控制」的同样情形就被用到了游戏、工作与购物上。

intro.en: The word began in Roman law, where it meant handing a person over.
intro.cn: 这个词起于罗马法，本义是把一个人交付出去。

items.en: dicere meant to say or to declare.
items.cn: dicere 意为说、宣告。

items.en: addicere meant to assign or to hand over.
items.cn: addicere 意为判定归属、交付。

items.en: addictio named the formal handing over of a person or thing.
items.cn: addictio 指正式把某人或某物交付出去。

items.en: addiction first meant devotion to a habit or pursuit.
items.cn: addiction 最初指对某种习惯或事务的投入。

items.en: medicine narrowed it to harmful dependence on drugs and later on behaviour.
items.cn: 医学把它收窄为对药物的有害依赖，后来又扩展到行为。

note.en: The first group shares the addict stem; the second names other forms of being tied to something.
note.cn: 第一组共享 addict 词干；第二组是别的表示「被某物拴住」的词。

normalIntro.en: Addict plus ion: the state of having been handed over to something.
normalIntro.cn: addict 加 ion：被交给某物之后所处的状态。

normal.en: The usual pattern is addiction to something.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 addiction to 某物。

normal.en: Drug addiction and alcohol addiction are the two medical staples.
normal.cn: drug addiction 与 alcohol addiction 是医学上的两个基本说法。

normal.en: The person is an addict, the state is addiction.
normal.cn: 人叫 addict，状态叫 addiction。

normal.en: Do not confuse addiction with addition; the second is simple arithmetic.
normal.cn: 别把 addiction 与 addition 混了，后者只是加法。

normal.en: The adjective addictive describes the thing, not the person.
normal.cn: 形容词 addictive 形容那个东西，而不是那个人。

abstract.en: See a hand reach again for a cup it does not need.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手又伸向那只并不需要的杯子。

abstract.en: Picture a screen glowing late at night and no one leaving it.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜亮着的屏幕，没有人离开。

abstract.en: Think of a chain that looks loose but will not come off.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看似松垮却摘不掉的链子。

examples.en: The clinic treats addiction as an illness, not a crime.
examples.cn: 这家诊所把成瘾当作疾病，而不是犯罪。

examples.en: His addiction to gambling cost him his savings.
examples.cn: 他的赌瘾让他失去了积蓄。

examples.en: She spoke openly about her addiction to work.
examples.cn: 她坦率地谈起自己对工作的沉迷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪克申」——阿迪一喝上就停不下来，家人带他去做戒瘾申报。

root: 拉丁语 addictio（正式交付），源自 addicere（判归、交付），由 ad（朝向）与 dicere（宣告）合成；由「把人交给某物」引申为对药物与行为的无法自控。

sensesIntro.en: One word covers drugs and games, because both take away control.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既管药物也管游戏，因为两者都夺走了控制权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for the same cup again.
core.cn: 核心意象：那只手又一次伸向同一个杯子。

branches.en: a body demanding a drug
branches.cn: 身体对药物的索求

branches.en: a mind returning to one activity
branches.cn: 心思反复回到同一件事

branches.en: dependence that harms health
branches.cn: 损害健康的依赖

branches.en: the same loss of control
branches.cn: 同一种失控

branches.en: a habit that behaves like a drug
branches.cn: 表现得像药物一样的习惯

intro.cn: 一个表示「交付」的拉丁动词，加一个表状态的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The same dicere gives dictate, predict and verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个 dicere 还给出 dictate、predict 与 verdict。

definition_zh: 松开；使变松；放松；放宽；变松
definition_en: to make something less tight, to relax a part of the body, to make rules or controls less strict, to weaken a connection, or to become less tight
core_image: 一只手捏住拧得太紧的瓶盖，慢慢往回拧，指节不再发白
scene: 厨房里，一只拧得太紧的瓶盖卡住了，他换了个手势慢慢往回拧。 He loosened the cap after a few turns and the jar opened easily.
sceneCN: 这里 loosen 是「松开、使变松」（第 1 个义项：让某物不再紧）；句意为拧了几圈后他把瓶盖拧松，罐子很容易打开。图中可辨识物件：厨房、瓶盖、罐子。

pos.zh: 松开；使变松；放松；放宽；变松

derivatives.zh: 由词基 loose 加 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；松散」
由 loosen 加 -ing 构成，义为「松开；放松的过程」

senses.title: To make something less tight
senses.definition: to reduce the tension on a fastening, a screw, a knot or a grip so that it can move or be removed
senses.definitionCN: 减小扣件、螺丝、绳结或握持上的张力，使它能够移动或被取下
senses.example: He loosened the lid with the help of a cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 他借一块布把盖子拧松了。
senses.why: The verb takes the adjective loose and adds the suffix -en, which means to make; the first sense is simply to put an object into that slack state.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词由形容词 loose 加后缀 -en 构成，而 -en 意为「使……」；第一个义项就是把某物放进那种松弛状态。

senses.title: To relax a part of the body
senses.definition: to make a muscle, joint or posture less tense
senses.definitionCN: 让肌肉、关节或姿势不再那么紧张
senses.example: Roll your shoulders and loosen your neck.
senses.exampleCN: 转一转肩膀，放松脖子。
senses.why: Muscles held too long become tight like a clamped fastening; relaxing them is the same reduction of tension applied to the body.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉保持太久会像卡紧的扣件一样发僵；放松它们，就是把同样的「减小张力」用在身体上。

senses.title: To make rules or controls less strict
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a rule, a limit or a form of control
senses.definitionCN: 减弱规则、限制或某种控制的力度
senses.example: The school loosened its dress code last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校去年放宽了着装规定。
senses.why: A rule works like a band holding behaviour in place; making it less strict is pictured as letting that band go slack.
senses.whyCN: 规则就像一条把行为固定住的带子；让规则不那么严，就被想成把这条带子放松。

senses.title: To weaken a connection or bond
senses.definition: to make a relationship, alliance or link less firm
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、联盟或联系变得不那么牢固
senses.example: Time and distance had loosened the bond between the old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 时间与距离让两位老朋友之间的情谊松动了。
senses.why: A bond is imagined as something tied; when it stops being tight, the people or groups it joined can move apart.
senses.whyCN: 情谊被想象成系在一起的东西；当它不再紧，被它连起来的人或群体就能彼此走开。

senses.title: To become less tight
senses.definition: of a fastening, grip or hold, to become less tight without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 指扣件、握持或抓握在没有外力的情况下自己变得不那么紧
senses.example: The rope loosened as the rain soaked through it.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水浸透之后，绳子自己松开了。
senses.why: The same verb covers both sides of the change: a hand can loosen a knot, and a wet knot can loosen on its own, because English does not mark who causes the slackening.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词覆盖变化的两端：手可以松开一个结，湿透的结也能自己变松，因为英语并不标明是谁造成了这种松弛。

intro.en: Loosen is an English verb built on the Germanic adjective loose plus a suffix meaning to make; it describes reduced tightness rather than complete freedom.
intro.cn: loosen 是由日耳曼语形容词 loose 加上表示「使……」的后缀构成的英语动词；它描述的是紧度减小，而不是彻底获得自由。

items.en: The family begins with the Germanic adjective for loose, generally traced to Old Norse lauss.
items.cn: 这个词族始于表示「松的」的日耳曼语形容词，一般认为可上溯到古诺斯语 lauss。

items.en: The reconstructed source also underlies German los and the English suffix -less.
items.cn: 重构的来源也支撑着德语 los 与英语后缀 -less。

items.en: Middle English had the adjective and a verb loose meaning to set free.
items.cn: 中古英语已有这个形容词，也有表示「释放」的动词 loose。

items.en: The verb suffix -en descends from Old English -nian and forms verbs such as strengthen, widen and loosen, meaning to make or become.
items.cn: 动词后缀 -en 源自古英语 -nian，构成 strengthen、widen、loosen 这类表示「使……、变得……」的动词。

items.en: Modern English keeps loosen for reducing tightness and loose for setting free, a division that the two words now share.
items.cn: 现代英语让 loosen 表示「减小紧度」，让 loose 表示「释放」，两个词如今分担了这一分工。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective, adverb and noun of the same family plus the confusing lose; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for reducing tension and strictness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、副词与名词，外加容易混淆的 lose；近义组收表示减小张力与严格程度的动词。

entries.definition: Not tight, not fitting closely, or free from restraint.
entries.definitionCN: 词基形容词兼动词，义为「松的；宽松的；不受约束的」。

entries.definition: In a slack, relaxed or inexact way.
entries.definitionCN: 同族副词，义为「松散地；不严格地」。

entries.definition: The quality or state of being loose.
entries.definitionCN: 同族名词，义为「松弛；松散」。

entries.definition: To no longer have something, or to fail to keep it.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写和读音相近，词源不同；义为「丢失；失去」。

entries.definition: To become or make less tense, active or fast.
entries.definitionCN: 变松；减慢；强调张力或速度下降，与 loosen 近义。

entries.definition: To make the body or a rule less tense or strict.
entries.definitionCN: 放松；放宽；多用于身体、规则与态度，不限于物理紧固。

entries.definition: To make something less difficult or less severe.
entries.definitionCN: 缓解；减轻；强调让困难或紧张变轻，不强调「松」这个动作。

entries.definition: To undo a knot or a binding.
entries.definitionCN: 解开；强调把结或捆绑完全解除，结果比 loosen 更彻底。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective loose plus the old suffix -en, and its family keeps returning to reduced tension rather than total release.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是形容词 loose 加上古老的 -en 后缀，同族词反复回到「减小张力」，而不是彻底释放。

normal.en: Loosen is loose plus -en, the suffix that means to make, so the verb means to make something loose.
normal.cn: loosen 是 loose 加 -en，这个后缀表示「使……」；所以动词的意思就是「使某物变松」。

normal.en: The -en suffix also builds strengthen and widen, which is why loosen belongs with verbs of change.
normal.cn: -en 后缀也构成 strengthen 与 widen，所以 loosen 属于表示变化的动词一类。

normal.en: Loosen a screw, loosen a knot, loosen a grip: each action reduces tension without removing the thing.
normal.cn: 拧松螺丝、松开绳结、放松握持：每个动作都减小张力，却没有把东西拿掉。

normal.en: Loosen up is what people do before exercise, letting tight muscles go slack.
normal.cn: loosen up 就是人们运动前做的事，让紧绷的肌肉松下来。

normal.en: Loose can also be a verb meaning to set free, but loosen is the everyday verb for making less tight.
normal.cn: loose 也能作动词表示「释放」，但 loosen 是日常用来表示「使变松」的动词。

abstract.en: A tight grip protects and controls, but it also tires the hand; loosening is how control makes room for rest.
abstract.cn: 紧握能保护与控制，但也会让手疲劳；松开就是控制为休息让出空间的方式。

abstract.en: Rules can be loosened without being removed, which is why the word describes pressure rather than absence.
abstract.cn: 规则可以被放宽而不必取消，所以这个词描述的是压力，而不是「没有规则」。

abstract.en: To loosen a knot is not to cut it; the rope remains, only the strain is gone.
abstract.cn: 松开一个结并不等于剪断它；绳子还在，只是张力没有了。

examples.en: The cap loosened after a few turns and the jar opened easily.
examples.cn: 拧了几圈后瓶盖松了，罐子很容易打开。

examples.en: He loosened the lid with the help of a cloth.
examples.cn: 他借一块布把盖子拧松了。

examples.en: Roll your shoulders and loosen your neck.
examples.cn: 转一转肩膀，放松脖子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卢森」——把拧紧的瓶盖慢慢拧回来，手就松了；loosen 就是松开、使变松。

root: loose（松的）加动词后缀 -en 构成；loose 一般认为源自古诺斯语 lauss（松的、自由的），属日耳曼语族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reduced tension; the senses divide into loosening an object, relaxing the body, relaxing rules, weakening a bond, and becoming loose by itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是张力减小；义项由此分出把物件弄松、放松身体、放宽规则、削弱联系，以及自己变松。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand slowly turning back a tight cap until the knuckles stop whitening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把拧得太紧的瓶盖慢慢往回拧，直到指节不再发白。

branches.en: a cap turning back under a hand
branches.cn: 一只手把瓶盖往回拧

branches.en: shoulders dropping after a long day
branches.cn: 忙了一天后肩膀垂下来

branches.en: a rule book left open to a softer line
branches.cn: 规则手册翻到较宽松的一页

branches.en: two friends drifting apart without a quarrel
branches.cn: 两位朋友没有争吵却渐渐疏远

branches.en: a wet knot slipping on its own
branches.cn: 湿透的绳结自己滑开

intro.en: The verb is the adjective loose plus the old suffix -en, and the family shares that base with loosely and looseness.
intro.cn: 这个动词是形容词 loose 加上古老的 -en 后缀，同族的 loosely 与 looseness 也共享这个词基。

latinIntro.en: Loosen is an English verb built on loose; the base belongs to Germanic stock, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
latinIntro.cn: loosen 是建立在 loose 之上的英语动词；词基属于日耳曼语族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 羊毛；毛线；毛料；毛纺织品
definition_en: the soft thick hair of sheep and some other animals, or the yarn and cloth made from it
core_image: 一大团刚从羊身上剪下的毛，捏一把会慢慢弹回来
scene: 冬天到了，奶奶翻出那团一直没用完的毛线，开始给孙辈织围巾。 This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
sceneCN: 这里 wool 是「羊毛、毛线」（第 1 个义项：羊身上柔软浓密的毛，也指用它纺成的线）；句意是这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。捏一把会慢慢弹回来的毛团，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 wool 加 -en 构成，义为「羊毛制的」
由 wool 加 -y 构成，义为「毛茸茸的；模糊的」
由 woolen 转作名词，义为「毛织品；毛料衣服」

senses.title: The fleece of the sheep
senses.definition: the soft thick hair that grows on sheep and some other animals, cut off once a year
senses.definitionCN: 羊及少数其他动物身上柔软浓密的毛，每年剪一次
senses.example: The farmer sells the wool from his sheep every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫每年春天卖掉羊身上的羊毛。
senses.why: This is the living source: the coat of the animal before anyone spins it.
senses.whyCN: 这是活的源头：还没被人纺过的动物皮毛。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: the yarn made by twisting the fibre, sold in balls for knitting
senses.definitionCN: 把纤维捻成的纱线，常以团为单位出售供编织
senses.example: Grandmother wound the wool into a ball before she started the scarf.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶先把毛线绕成团，才动手织围巾。
senses.why: Once the fibre is twisted, the same word follows it into the ball on the table.
senses.whyCN: 纤维一旦被捻成线，这个词就跟着它走进桌上那团线里。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: the cloth woven from the yarn, used for coats and suits
senses.definitionCN: 用这种线织成的布料，用于外套和西装
senses.example: This sweater is pure wool, so it stays warm even when it gets wet.
senses.exampleCN: 这件毛衣是纯羊毛的，湿了也仍然暖和。
senses.why: From the ball to the loom is one more step, and the material name covers the finished cloth too.
senses.whyCN: 从线团到织机只差一步，材料名便也涵盖了织成的布。

senses.title: Being pulled back
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase "pull the wool over someone's eyes", meaning to trick them
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定说法「pull the wool over someone's eyes」，意即欺骗某人
senses.example: He tried to pull the wool over her eyes, but she had checked the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他想蒙骗她，但她早已核过数字。
senses.why: The soft fibre of a wig or a hood once hid the eyes, so the material stands for a blindfold.
senses.whyCN: 早年假发或兜帽的柔软毛料会遮住眼睛，于是这种材料成了蒙眼布的代称。

intro.en: Wool is Old English wull, shared with German Wolle and Dutch wol, and going back to a reconstructed root for the fleece.
intro.cn: wool 来自古英语 wull，与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源，可上溯到一个表示羊毛的重构词根。

items.en: wull named the fleece of the sheep and the cloth made from it.
items.cn: wull 指羊的毛以及用它制成的布。

items.en: The same word for fleece appears across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 相同的「羊毛」一词出现在各门日耳曼语中。

items.en: The vowel shortened and the spelling settled on wool.
items.cn: 元音变短，拼写固定为 wool。

items.en: The endings -en and -y built woollen and woolly.
items.cn: 词尾 -en 与 -y 造出 woollen 与 woolly。

items.en: Idioms such as "pull the wool over someone's eyes" fixed the word in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「pull the wool over someone's eyes」之类的成语让这个词进入日常口语。

note.en: The first group holds the forms built on the same stem, the second holds other textile words that often meet it.
note.cn: 第一组收同根构成的词形，第二组收常与它相遇的其他纺织词。

normalIntro.en: Wool is a short native word with a doubled vowel spelling but a single short sound.
normalIntro.cn: wool 是一个简短的本土词，两个 o 只读一个短音。

normal.en: Two o letters, one short vowel sound: wool rhymes with full.
normal.cn: 两个 o 只读一个短元音：wool 与 full 押韵。

normal.en: Woollen and woolen are two spellings of the same adjective, British and American.
normal.cn: woollen 与 woolen 是同一个形容词的英式与美式拼写。

normal.en: Woolly doubles the l before -y; the other spelling keeps -en instead.
normal.cn: woolly 在 -y 前双写 l；另一种拼写则用 -en。

normal.en: Cotton wool is not wool at all, which shows how the word can mean soft fibre in general.
normal.cn: cotton wool 根本不是羊毛，可见这个词也可泛指柔软的纤维。

normal.en: The idiom "pull the wool over his eyes" comes from a soft cloth hiding the eyes.
normal.cn: 成语「pull the wool over his eyes」源自用软布遮眼。

abstract.en: A handful of fleece that slowly springs back into shape.
abstract.cn: 一把羊毛慢慢弹回原样。

abstract.en: The smell of a sweater dried near a fire.
abstract.cn: 在火边烘干的毛衣的气味。

abstract.en: A year of warmth carried in two hands.
abstract.cn: 一整年的温暖捧在两只手里。

examples.en: This coat is lined with thick wool for the winter.
examples.cn: 这件外套用厚羊毛做衬，适合冬天。

examples.en: She bought three balls of wool to knit a scarf.
examples.cn: 她买了三团毛线来织围巾。

examples.en: Nobody could pull the wool over his eyes after that mistake.
examples.cn: 出了那次错以后，谁也别想蒙他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捂」——冬天用羊毛把脖子捂得严严的。

root: 古英语 wull（羊毛），与德语 Wolle、荷兰语 wol 同源；-en 与 -y 分别构成 woollen、woolly。

sensesIntro.en: The fleece comes first, then the thread twisted from it, then the cloth woven from the thread, and finally the soft blindfold of an idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是羊毛，再是捻成的线，接着是织成的布，最后是那句成语里的软蒙眼布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of fleece springing back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把会弹回来的羊毛。

branches.en: The source branch: wool sold from the farm each spring.
branches.cn: 源头分支：农场每年春天卖羊毛。

branches.en: The yarn branch: a ball of wool before knitting.
branches.cn: 纱线分支：织之前的线团。

branches.en: The cloth branch: a coat that stays warm when wet.
branches.cn: 布料分支：湿了也暖的外套。

branches.en: The trick branch: the soft cloth over the eyes.
branches.cn: 欺骗分支：遮在眼前的软布。

branches.cn: 材料分支：一个词从羊到外套。

intro.cn: wool 是裸词干；-en 与 -y 是把它变成形容词的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below name wool or fleece from another branch.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词从另一支来指羊毛。

definition_zh: 不友好的；冷淡的；不友善的；不利的
definition_en: not kind or welcoming to others, or not helpful to something
core_image: 门口挂着牌子，人一走近就把窗帘拉上
scene: 新搬来的邻居遇到楼道里迎面走来的人，笑着点头，对方却目不斜视地走过去。 The neighbours were polite but unfriendly.
sceneCN: 这里 unfriendly 是「冷淡的、不友好的」（第 1 个义项：对人缺乏善意）；句意为邻居们客气但冷淡。人一靠近就拉上窗帘，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不友好；冷淡」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「友好的」
词族核心名词，义为「朋友」
肯定形式加 -ness 的名词，义为「友善」

senses.title: Cold in manner towards others
senses.definition: behaving in a cold or unwelcoming way towards other people
senses.definitionCN: 以冷淡、不欢迎的方式对待他人
senses.example: The shop assistant was unfriendly but not rude.
senses.exampleCN: 那个店员不友好，却还没到粗鲁的地步。
senses.why: The prefix turns friendly inside out, so the quality of a friend is exactly what is missing.
senses.whyCN: 前缀把 friendly（像朋友一样的）翻了个面，缺的正是朋友那份情谊。

senses.title: A place or group that gives no warmth
senses.definition: used of a place, crowd, or atmosphere that makes people feel unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个场所、人群或气氛让人觉得自己不受欢迎
senses.example: The club had an unfriendly feel, all dark wood and low voices.
senses.exampleCN: 那个俱乐部气氛冷淡，全是深色木饰和低低的说话声。
senses.why: A room takes its mood from the people in it, so a cold crowd makes a cold place.
senses.whyCN: 屋子从人身上取得气氛，人冷淡，地方也就冷。

senses.title: Harsh or hostile in a look or tone
senses.definition: used of a gaze, tone, or remark that shows dislike
senses.definitionCN: 形容流露出反感的眼神、语气或话语
senses.example: He gave the newcomer an unfriendly stare.
senses.exampleCN: 他不友善地盯着新来的人。
senses.why: Whatever warmth would lie in a greeting is reversed, and the face closes.
senses.whyCN: 本该在问候里的那份暖意被反转，脸上就关起了门。

senses.title: Working against something
senses.titleCN: 不利的；不友好的（技术、环境语境）
senses.definition: used of systems, designs, or policies that are hard on users or the environment
senses.definitionCN: 形容对使用者或环境不友善的系统、设计或政策
senses.example: Critics called the new form user-unfriendly and needlessly long.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说新表格对使用者不友好，而且长得没有必要。
senses.why: The everyday sense of not being kind moves easily onto things that treat people badly.
senses.whyCN: 日常语中「不厚道」的意思，很容易挪到苛待人的事物上。

senses.title: Not favourable to a cause
senses.definition: used of conditions or attitudes that oppose a plan or interest
senses.definitionCN: 形容不利于某项计划或利益的条件与态度
senses.example: The town proved unfriendly to new businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 事实证明，这个镇子对新企业并不友好。
senses.why: Anything that receives you coldly makes your work harder, so unfriendly also means unfavourable.
senses.whyCN: 任何冷脸相迎的东西都会让你的工作更难，于是「不友好」也等于「不利」。

intro.en: Friendly is an English adjective on the old Germanic noun friend, with the negative prefix added.
intro.cn: friendly 是古日耳曼语名词 friend 派生的英语形容词，否定前缀是后加的。

items.en: Freond meant a friend, from a Germanic root meaning to love.
items.cn: freond 意为「朋友」，词根在日耳曼语中表示「爱」。

items.en: The noun carried duties as well as affection, as in a friend in need.
items.cn: 这个名词除情谊外还带着义务，如患难中的朋友。

items.en: Freendly appeared as an adjective describing kind behaviour.
items.cn: freendly 作为形容词出现，描写厚道的举止。

items.en: Un- was added to describe the opposite temper, often of looks and places.
items.cn: 加 un- 表示相反的性格，常用于神情与场所。

items.en: Modern compounds extend it to designs and policies, as in user-unfriendly.
items.cn: 现代的复合词又把它扩展到设计与政策，如 user-unfriendly。

note.en: The look-alike group is the friend family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for coldness.
note.cn: 形近组是 friend 词族，近义组汇集表示冷淡的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is friend turned into an adjective and then turned against itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 friend 先变成形容词，又被反过来用。

normal.en: Un- plus friendly: without the warmth of a friend.
normal.cn: un- 加 friendly：没有朋友的那份暖意。

normal.en: Be unfriendly to someone is the usual preposition.
normal.cn: be unfriendly to someone 是常见的介词搭配。

normal.en: User-unfriendly shows how a manner word moves onto objects.
normal.cn: user-unfriendly 显示了方式类形容词如何移到器物上。

normal.cn: 这里的 -ly 构成形容词，与 lovely、costly 同理。

normal.en: Unfriendliness is the noun, though most people use coldness instead.
normal.cn: 名词是 unfriendliness，不过多数人更常说 coldness。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain drawn the moment footsteps reach the door.
abstract.cn: 想象脚步声刚到门口，窗帘就被拉上。

abstract.en: See a nod that stops half way.
abstract.cn: 看一个点到一半就收住的头。

abstract.en: Hear a greeting answered with a single flat syllable.

examples.en: The staff were not rude, just unfriendly.

examples.en: An unfriendly silence greeted his joke.
examples.cn: 他的笑话只换来一片冷淡的沉默。

examples.en: The tax rules are unfriendly to small firms.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺勿弗伦德利」——俺没把人家当朋友待，人家自然也不给好脸。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ friendly，friendly 由古英语 freond（朋友）派生，词根在日耳曼语中表示「爱」

sensesIntro.en: One missing warmth spreads from faces to rooms, to the look in an eye, and to rules and forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份缺席的暖意，从脸上蔓延到屋子、眼神，再到规则与表格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain pulled shut as someone walks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人走近时被拉上的窗帘。

branches.en: The personal branch: the person who does not meet your eyes.
branches.cn: 个人分支：不与你对视的那个人。

branches.en: The place branch: a room that feels shut.
branches.cn: 场所分支：让人感到关起来的房间。

branches.en: The expression branch: the stare and the flat tone.
branches.cn: 神情分支：那道目光与平板的语气。

branches.en: The technical branch: forms and conditions that work against you.
branches.cn: 技术分支：与你作对的表格与条件。

branches.en: The plain everyday sense most learners meet first.
branches.cn: 学习者最先遇到的最朴素的日常义。

intro.en: A native English noun, an adjective ending, and a negative prefix make up the word.
intro.cn: 本土英语名词、形容词词尾与否定前缀共同构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer; friend is Germanic, so the Latin list is empty.

items.meaning: a person you love and trust

items.exampleCN: 新应用对使用者不友好。
一群带有敌意的人聚集在外面。

definition_zh: 误导；使误解；带错路；使产生错误印象
definition_en: to cause someone to believe something that is not true; to guide a person along the wrong way; and of a thing, to give a false impression
core_image: 路口一块指向反方向的木牌，行人照着箭头走进雾里
scene: 山路口立着一块被人转反的木牌，几个行人照着箭头走进雾里，越走越偏。 A single confusing sign can mislead even an experienced driver.
sceneCN: 这里是「带错路」（第 2 个义项：指错方向）；句意为一块让人困惑的路牌，即使经验丰富的司机也会被带错方向。图中可辨识物件：转反的木牌、雾、走进雾里的行人。

pos.zh: 误导；使误解；带错路；使产生错误印象

derivatives.zh: 由 mislead 加 -ing 构成，义为「误导性的；引入歧途的」
由 misleading 加 -ly 构成，义为「以误导的方式」

senses.title: To cause someone to believe something false
senses.definition: to make someone accept an untrue idea, often without any deliberate intention to lie
senses.definitionCN: 使某人把不真实的想法当成真的，常常并非有意撒谎
senses.example: The advertisement misleads buyers about the true cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告在真实花费上误导了买家。
senses.why: Mis- marks a wrong turn and lead is the act of guiding, so mislead is guidance that ends in a false belief rather than in a false place.
senses.whyCN: mis- 标出一个错误的方向，lead 是引领的动作，所以 mislead 是把人引向错误信念的引导，而不只是把路带错。

senses.title: To guide someone along the wrong way
senses.definition: to lead a person or group along a wrong route, or away from the place they meant to reach
senses.definitionCN: 把人或一群人带到错误的路线，或带离他们原本要去的地方
senses.example: The old map misled us into a dead-end valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那张旧地图把我们带进了一条没有出口的山谷。
senses.why: Before it described deceiving the mind, the word described taking someone by the hand and walking them the wrong way, and that physical sense still survives beside the mental one.
senses.whyCN: 在用来描述蒙蔽头脑之前，这个词说的是牵着人走错路；这一身体层面的意思至今仍与头脑层面的意思并存。

senses.title: To give a false impression of something
senses.definition: of an appearance, a result or a piece of evidence, to suggest something that is not actually the case
senses.definitionCN: 指外表、结果或证据让人以为某事成立，而事实并非如此
senses.example: The first results misled the researchers into expecting a quick cure.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的结果让研究人员误以为很快就能找到疗法。
senses.why: If a person can be led astray, so can an observer's judgement; the word then describes evidence that pulls the mind down a wrong path without anyone telling a lie.
senses.whyCN: 既然人能被人带偏，观察者的判断也能被带偏；于是这个词描述的是把头脑拽上错误路径的证据，即使没有谁说谎。

intro.en: Mislead is an Old English compound of mis-, meaning wrong, and lædan, to lead; its past tense misled still hides an irregular vowel change.
intro.cn: mislead 是古英语中用 mis-（错误）与 lædan（引领）构成的复合词；它的过去式 misled 仍保留着不规则的元音变化。

items.en: The prefix mis- meant wrong, badly or astray, and it was freely added to English verbs.
items.cn: 前缀 mis- 意为错误、不当、走偏，可以自由地加在英语动词前面。

items.en: Lædan meant to lead or to bring a person along a way, and it is the verb behind modern lead.
items.cn: lædan 意为引领、把人带在路上走，是现代 lead 背后的动词。

items.en: Mislædan joined the two parts and meant to lead astray, first in the literal sense of a wrong road.
items.cn: mislædan 把两部分组合起来，意为引人入歧途，最初是字面意义上的走错路。

items.en: Middle English kept the literal sense and began to use the word for leading someone's mind into error.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了字面义，并开始用这个词表示把人的想法引入错误。

items.en: Modern English uses mislead mostly for false beliefs and false impressions, while the wrong-road sense stays in the background.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用 mislead 表示错误信念与错误印象，而「带错路」的意思退到了背景里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and relatives of mislead plus one word built on the same prefix; the near-meaning group collects verbs for guiding someone into error.
note.cn: 形近组收 mislead 的各种形式与同族词，外加一个用同一前缀构成的词；近义组收表示把人引向错误的动词。

entries.definition: Giving a false impression; the present participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 给人错误印象的；现在分词用作形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of mislead.
entries.definitionCN: mislead 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: In a way that gives a false impression.
entries.definitionCN: 以给人错误印象的方式。

entries.definition: To give someone wrong information; it shares the prefix mis- but uses inform.
entries.definitionCN: 向某人提供错误信息；共用前缀 mis-，但词干是 inform。

entries.definition: To make someone believe something false, usually on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人相信不真实的事，通常是有意的。

entries.definition: To make someone do or believe something by a clever ruse.
entries.definitionCN: 用巧妙的手段让人做某事或相信某事。

entries.definition: To guide someone badly or along a wrong course.
entries.definitionCN: 把人带坏或引向错误方向。

entries.definition: To send someone or something in the wrong direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物送往错误的方向。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of a Germanic prefix for wrongness and the verb to lead; its family keeps returning to guidance that ends somewhere nobody meant to go.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的日耳曼语前缀与动词「引领」构成，同族词反复回到通向谁都不想去之处的引导。

normal.en: Mislead is made of mis-, wrong, and lead, to guide, so the word pictures guidance that ends in error.
normal.cn: mislead 由 mis-（错误）与 lead（引领）构成，所以这个词画出的是以错误收场的引导。

normal.en: Lead is an Old English verb, which is why the past tense is misled and not misleaded.
normal.cn: lead 是古英语动词，所以过去式是 misled，而不是 misleaded。

normal.en: Misled looks like a different word but is simply the past form, made by changing the vowel rather than adding -ed.
normal.cn: misled 看起来像另一个词，其实只是过去式，靠换元音而不是加 -ed 构成。

normal.en: Misleading keeps the same idea for things rather than people: a sign, a result or a statistic can lead the mind astray.
normal.cn: misleading 把同样的意思用在物而不是人身上：路牌、结果或统计数据都能把头脑带偏。

normal.en: Misinform shares the prefix mis- but uses inform instead of lead, so the two words describe error delivered as news and error delivered as guidance.
normal.cn: misinform 共用前缀 mis-，但词干是 inform 而不是 lead，于是两个词分别描述以消息形式送来的错误和以引导形式送来的错误。

abstract.en: A reversed signpost is the whole story: nobody lied to the traveller, yet the road still ends in the wrong place.
abstract.cn: 一块转反的路牌就是全部故事：没有谁对旅人说谎，路却仍然通向错误的地方。

abstract.en: The word keeps body and mind in one frame, since a wrong road and a false belief are both reached by following someone.
abstract.cn: 这个词把身体与头脑放在同一幅画里，因为走错的路与信错的念头都是跟着别人走到的。

abstract.en: Because mislead often needs no intention to lie, it can describe a result as easily as it describes a liar.
abstract.cn: 因为 mislead 常常不需要撒谎的意图，它既能形容一个骗子，也能同样轻松地形容一个结果。

examples.en: The advertisement misleads buyers about the true cost.
examples.cn: 这则广告在真实花费上误导了买家。

examples.en: The old map misled us into a dead-end valley.
examples.cn: 那张旧地图把我们带进了一条没有出口的山谷。

examples.en: The first results misled the researchers into expecting a quick cure.
examples.cn: 最初的结果让研究人员误以为很快就能找到疗法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米斯立德」——米斯把人领到一条错路上；记住 mislead 是误导、带错路。

root: 古英语 mis-（错误）加 lædan（引领）构成 mislædan，意为「带错路」，后引申为「把人的想法引向错误」；lead 属于日耳曼语，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is guidance that ends in error; the senses divide into a false belief, a literal wrong route, and evidence that gives a false impression.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是通向错误的引导；义项分为错误信念、字面意义上的错路，以及造成错误印象的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost turned the wrong way, walkers following its arrow into the fog and drifting further off.
core.cn: 核心意象：路口一块指向反方向的木牌，行人照着箭头走进雾里，越走越偏。

branches.en: a walker following a reversed sign into fog
branches.cn: 跟着转反的路牌走进雾里的行人

branches.en: a buyer trusting a price that hides its extras
branches.cn: 买家相信一个藏了附加费的价格

branches.en: a first result pointing at a cure that is not there
branches.cn: 最初结果指向一个并不存在的疗法

branches.en: a hand on the shoulder steering someone off the path
branches.cn: 搭在肩上的手把人引离小路

branches.en: a compass and a chart both pointing wrong
branches.cn: 指南针与海图都指错了方向

intro.en: The word is carried by the Germanic prefix for wrongness, the Old English verb to lead, its modern form and the endings that build the adjective and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示错误的日耳曼语前缀、古英语中表示引领的动词、它的现代形式，以及构成形容词与副词的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for mislead: both mis- and lead belong to the Germanic branch, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: mislead 没有可靠的拉丁同族词：mis- 与 lead 都属于日耳曼语这一支，因此拉丁同源部分留空。

definition_zh: 污渍；染色；玷污
definition_en: a dirty mark, to colour something, or to damage a reputation
core_image: 桌布上一块深色的墨水渍
scene: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。 The ink left a stain on the cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 stain 是「污渍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

senses.title: Dirty mark
senses.definition: a dirty mark that is hard to remove
senses.definitionCN: 难以去除的脏痕
senses.example: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。
senses.why: This is the everyday physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常最常用的具体义项。

senses.title: Colour wood or cloth
senses.definition: to give colour to wood or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 给木材或织物上色
senses.example: They stained the wood dark brown.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把木头染成深棕色。
senses.why: A stain can be wanted, not just dirt.
senses.whyCN: 染色可以是有意为之，而不只是脏污。

senses.title: Damage a name
senses.definition: to damage someone's reputation
senses.definitionCN: 损害某人的名声
senses.example: The scandal stained his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。
senses.why: A mark on cloth became a mark on character.
senses.whyCN: 布上的印记变成了人格上的污点。

intro.en: Stain comes from Old French desteindre, to take colour away, from Latin tingere, to dye.
intro.cn: stain 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）。

items.en: Tingere meant to dye or wet.
items.cn: tingere 意为染色或浸湿。

items.en: Desteindre meant to take colour away.
items.cn: desteindre 意为使褪色。

items.en: Stain meant to discolour or spot.
items.cn: stain 意为使变色、留下斑点。

items.en: The noun named the mark itself.
items.cn: 名词义指印记本身。

items.en: The moral sense grew from visible marks.
items.cn: 道德义由可见的印记引申而来。

note.en: Stain is compared with look-alike words and words for marks.
note.cn: 把 stain 与形近词以及表示印记的词作比较。

a raised floor for performing
the people who work somewhere
a small visible spot
a small round mark

normalIntro.en: Stain is a mark left behind, whether on cloth, wood, or a name.
normalIntro.cn: stain 是留下的印记，无论在布上、木上，还是在名声上。

normal.en: There is a stain on your shirt.
normal.cn: 你衬衫上有一块污渍。

normal.en: Use soap on the stain.
normal.cn: 在污渍上抹点肥皂。

normal.en: They stained the floor brown.
normal.cn: 他们把地板染成棕色。

normal.en: The window has stained glass.
normal.cn: 这扇窗装着彩色玻璃。

normal.en: The lie stained his reputation.
normal.cn: 谎言玷污了他的名声。

abstract.en: Some marks wash out; some do not.
abstract.cn: 有些印记洗得掉，有些洗不掉。

abstract.en: Colour and dirt share one word.
abstract.cn: 色彩与污垢，共用一个词。

abstract.en: A name, once stained, keeps the shape of the mark.
abstract.cn: 名声一旦被玷污，就留下印记的形状。

examples.en: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
examples.cn: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

examples.en: They stained the wood dark brown.
examples.cn: 他们把木头染成深棕色。

examples.en: The scandal stained his name.
examples.cn: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。

dict_mnemonic.text: stain 是「污渍」，也指「染色、玷污」；coffee stain 是咖啡渍，stain remover 是去污剂，stained glass 是彩色玻璃；stainless 是不锈的。

root: 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）；由「使布变色」引申为污渍、有意染色，再引申为玷污名声。

sensesIntro.en: Stain means a dirty mark, the act of colouring, or damage to a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: stain 指污渍、染色，或对名声的玷污。

core.en: A colour mark left on a surface.
core.cn: 留在表面上的颜色印记。

branches.en: Ink spreads into a dark patch.
branches.cn: 墨水晕开成一块深色印记。

branches.en: A brush lays colour on wood.
branches.cn: 刷子把颜色涂在木头上。

branches.en: Whispers leave a shadow on a name.
branches.cn: 流言在名声上留下阴影。

branches.en: The same mark may be dirt or design.
branches.cn: 同一个印记，可能是污垢，也可能是设计。

branches.en: Cloth and character both keep a mark.
branches.cn: 布匹与人格，都会留下印记。

intro.en: Stain forms verb parts and a family of colour words.
intro.cn: stain 构成动词变化以及一组与颜色相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is tingere, to dye.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 tingere，意为染色。

items.example: The stain will not come out.
There are stains on the rug.
Staining the table takes a day.

items.exampleCN: 两名染色工在那里干活。

definition_zh: 保护；保存；节约
definition_en: the protection of nature and old things, or the careful use of resources
core_image: 护林员把幼苗周围的杂草轻轻拨开
scene: 护林员在幼苗周围插上木牌，请游人绕行。 The conservation of the old forest took thirty years.
sceneCN: 这里 conservation 指「保护」（第 1 个义项：对自然或古迹的保护）；句意是这片古老森林的保护工作持续了三十年。

senses.title: Protecting nature
senses.definition: the protection of animals, plants and natural places
senses.definitionCN: 对动植物与自然环境的保护
senses.example: The conservation of the old forest took thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这片古老森林的保护工作持续了三十年。
senses.why: A living place survives only if someone guards it on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 一片有生命的土地，只有被有意守护才能存续。

senses.title: Careful use
senses.definition: the careful use of resources so that they are not wasted
senses.definitionCN: 对资源的节约使用，避免浪费
senses.example: Water conservation begins at home.
senses.exampleCN: 节约用水从家里开始。
senses.why: What is used slowly lasts longer than what is spent fast.
senses.whyCN: 慢慢用的东西，比快速耗掉的东西用得久。

senses.title: Keeping in good condition
senses.definition: the work of keeping old buildings or objects in good condition
senses.definitionCN: 使旧建筑或旧物保持良好状态的工作
senses.example: The conservation of the wall took months.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙的修复用了好几个月。
senses.why: Old things do not stay old by accident; someone stops the decay.
senses.whyCN: 旧东西不会自己保持原样，总有人拦住了腐朽。

intro.en: Conservation comes from Latin conservatio, a keeping together, from com-, together, and servare, to keep safe.
intro.cn: conservation 来自拉丁语 conservatio，意为共同守护，由 com-（一起）与 servare（保全）构成。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe or to watch over.
items.cn: servare 意为保全或看守。

items.en: Conservare meant to keep something whole and unharmed.
items.cn: conservare 意为使某物保持完整无损。

items.en: Conservatio named the act of guarding and keeping.
items.cn: conservatio 指守护与保存的行为。

items.en: Old French conservation carried the keeping sense.
items.cn: 古法语 conservation 带有保存的含义。

items.en: English conservation first meant preservation from harm.
items.cn: 英语 conservation 最初指免于损害的保存。

items.en: It now covers nature, energy and old buildings.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖自然、能源与古老建筑。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of conservation, and the meaning group names other kinds of keeping safe.
note.cn: 形近组与 conservation 读音相近，近义组列出其他表示保护保存的词。

entries.definition: a talk between two or more people
entries.definitionCN: 两人或多人之间的谈话

entries.definition: an arrangement to keep a seat or room
a person who works to protect nature
the act of keeping something in its original state
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持原状的行为

entries.definition: the act of keeping something safe from harm
entries.definitionCN: 使某物免受伤害的行为

entries.definition: the work and cost of maintaining something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from hands clearing weeds, then move to a tap turned off and to an old wall being repaired.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从拨开杂草的手开始，再到拧紧的水龙头，最后到正在修复的旧墙。

normal.en: Con- is together and serv- is keep, so conservation is keeping something safe for everyone.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，serv- 是保存，conservation 就是大家一起把某物守住。

normal.en: A guard who walks the forest every morning is conservation in boots.
normal.cn: 每天早晨巡林的护林员，就是穿着靴子的保护工作。

normal.en: Turning off the tap is conservation with one hand.
