definition_zh: 侄子；外甥；姻亲的侄甥；旧指孙子、后裔
definition_en: the son of your brother or sister, or of your husband's or wife's sibling; in older use, a male descendant
core_image: 院门口的葡萄架下放着一只旧行李箱，一个半大男孩站在门廊上等长辈开口
scene: 暑假第一天的傍晚，院门口的葡萄架下放着一只旧行李箱，男孩正和长辈打招呼。 My nephew will stay with us for three weeks this summer.
sceneCN: 这里是「侄子／外甥」（第 1 个义项：兄弟姐妹的儿子）；句意为我的侄子这个夏天要在我们这儿住三个星期。图中可辨识物件：葡萄架、旧行李箱、门廊。

pos.zh: 侄子；外甥；姻亲的侄甥；旧指孙子、后裔

derivatives.zh: 与 nephew 同出拉丁亲属词，是阴性对应词，义为「侄女；外甥女」
由拉丁词干 nepot-（侄子、孙子）加 -ism 构成，义为「任人唯亲」
由 nepotism 加 -ic 构成，义为「任人唯亲的；偏袒亲属的」

senses.title: The son of your brother or sister
senses.definition: a boy or man who is the son of your brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的儿子
senses.example: My nephew will stay with us for three weeks this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 我的侄子这个夏天要在我们这儿住三个星期。
senses.why: Latin nepos covered both grandson and nephew, so English inherited one word for a young male kinsman one generation below the speaker, without asking which parent supplied the link.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nepos 同时指孙子和侄子，英语因此只继承了一个词，用来指比自己低一辈的男性亲属，并不追问是哪位长辈带来的这层关系。

senses.title: The son of your spouse's sibling
senses.titleCN: 姻亲的侄甥；配偶那边的侄子
senses.definition: the son of your husband's or wife's brother or sister, related by marriage rather than by blood
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫或妻子的兄弟姐妹的儿子，靠婚姻而非血缘联系起来
senses.example: Her nephew came to the wedding with his parents.
senses.exampleCN: 她的侄子跟着父母来参加了婚礼。
senses.why: Marriage folds two family trees together, and English simply applies the existing kinship word to the partner's side, so no new form is needed for a nephew acquired through a spouse.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻把两棵家族树并到一起，英语直接把已有的亲属词用到伴侣那一边，所以因配偶而得到的侄子并不需要另造一个词。

senses.title: A male descendant, in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, a grandson or any male descendant, not only a sibling's son
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文本中指孙子或任何男性后裔，而不只指兄弟姐妹的儿子
senses.example: In the old chronicle, the king named his nephew as heir.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，国王指定他的孙子为继承人。
senses.why: The Latin word meant grandson before it meant nephew, and early English kept that wider sense until grandson and cousin took over the narrower jobs and left nephew with its modern range.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词先指孙子，后指侄子；早期英语保留了较宽的意思，直到 grandson 与 cousin 接走那些更窄的职责，才把 nephew 留在今天的范围里。

intro.en: Nephew goes back to a Latin word that named a grandson as well as a nephew, and it reached English through French with its family range already narrowed.
intro.cn: nephew 可追到既指孙子又指侄子的拉丁词，经法语进入英语时，它的亲属范围已经收窄。

items.en: Nepos meant a grandson and also a nephew, and its stem nepot- survives in words about favour shown to relatives.
items.cn: nepos 既指孙子也指侄子，其词干 nepot- 留在表示「偏袒亲属」的词里。

items.en: Neptis was the matching feminine noun for a granddaughter, and it is the source of the English word for a sibling's daughter.
items.cn: neptis 是相配的阴性名词，指孙女，也是英语中「侄女、外甥女」一词的来源。

items.en: Old French narrowed the Latin word to neveu, the son of a sibling, and passed the form to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词收窄为 neveu，专指兄弟姐妹的儿子，并在诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as neveu or nevew, and spellings with ph appeared later under the influence of the Latin stem nepot-.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 neveu 或 nevew，带 ph 的拼写是后来受拉丁词干 nepot- 影响才出现的。

items.en: Modern English keeps nephew for a sibling's son, adds the in-law sense, and leaves the older grandson sense to historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语用 nephew 指兄弟姐妹的儿子，添上姻亲义，把较旧的「孙子」义留给历史写作。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the learned words built on the same Latin stem of kinship; the near-meaning group holds the other names for close family members.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁亲属词干上造出的书面词；近义组收其他表示近亲称谓的词。

entries.definition: The practice of giving jobs or favours to relatives, built on the Latin stem for nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 把职位或好处给亲属的做法，建在表示「侄子」的拉丁词干上。

entries.definition: A person who favours relatives in appointments or business.
entries.definitionCN: 在任用或生意中偏袒亲属的人。

entries.definition: Showing favouritism towards relatives, formed from nepotism with -ic.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出对亲属偏袒的，由 nepotism 加 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: The daughter of your brother or sister, the female counterpart of nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的女儿，是 nephew 的阴性对应词。

entries.definition: The child of your aunt or uncle, another kinsman of your own generation.
entries.definitionCN: 姑舅姨伯的孩子，同辈的另一类亲属。

entries.definition: A person connected to you by blood or marriage, the general term above nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻与你相连的人，是覆盖 nephew 的上位词。

entries.definition: A male relative, used in older or literary English.
entries.definitionCN: 男性亲属，多用于较旧或文学性的英语。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin kinship noun that French narrowed, and its relatives keep the same picture of a younger male in the family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语收窄过的拉丁亲属名词，它的同族词都保留着「家族中较年幼男性」的画面。

normal.en: Latin nepos meant both grandson and nephew, so the English word started with a wider family range than it now has.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nepos 兼指孙子与侄子，所以英语这个词一开始的亲属范围比现在宽。

normal.en: French reduced the Latin word to neveu, and English respelled it with ph because the Latin stem nepot- was still visible in learned words.
normal.cn: 法语把拉丁词缩成 neveu，英语又用 ph 改写，因为拉丁词干 nepot- 在书面词里仍然看得见。

normal.en: Niece is the matching word from Latin neptis, so nephew and niece are two branches of one Latin family rather than unrelated labels.
normal.cn: niece 是来自拉丁语 neptis 的对应词，所以 nephew 与 niece 是同一拉丁词族的两支，而不是两个互不相干的称呼。

normal.en: Nepotism comes from the same stem: favour handed to a nephew is the literal picture behind the modern word for favouritism.
normal.cn: nepotism 出自同一词干：把好处递给侄子，正是现代「任人唯亲」一词背后的字面画面。

normal.en: The in-law sense needs no new form, because English simply applies the existing kinship word to the spouse's side of the family.
normal.cn: 姻亲义不需要新形式，因为英语直接把已有的亲属词用到配偶那一边的家族。

abstract.en: A single Latin word once held a grandson and a nephew, and English kept the narrower half that everyday family life needed.
abstract.cn: 一个拉丁词曾同时装下孙子和侄子，英语只留下日常家庭生活更需要的窄的那一半。

abstract.en: A word for a boy in the family turns into a word for favouritism, because the nearest relative is also the easiest person to help.
abstract.cn: 一个指家族男孩的词变成了「任人唯亲」，因为最近的亲属也往往是最容易帮的人。

abstract.en: Nephew and niece are mirror images from one old stem, which is why the pair sounds balanced even though the endings differ.
abstract.cn: nephew 与 niece 是同一个古老词干的两面镜子，所以这对词尽管词尾不同，听起来仍然对称。

examples.en: My nephew is learning to ride a bicycle.
examples.cn: 我的侄子正在学骑自行车。

examples.en: She brought her nephew to the family dinner.
examples.cn: 她把侄子带来参加家庭聚餐。

examples.en: Their nephew by marriage stayed for the whole holiday.
examples.cn: 他们姻亲那边的侄子整个假期都住在他们家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「涅夫尤」——叔伯家的男孩来了，喊一声就去开门；nephew 就是侄子、外甥。

root: 拉丁语 nepos（孙子；侄子，词干 nepot-）经古法语 neveu 进入英语；同族词 niece 来自拉丁语 neptis，nepotism 也出自同一词干。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a younger male kinsman; the senses then separate by blood, by marriage, and by the older use that still included grandsons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是比自己低一辈的男性亲属；义项随后按血缘、按婚姻，以及仍包含孙子的旧用法分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boy with a suitcase standing under a grape trellis, waiting for an older relative to speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个提着行李箱的男孩站在葡萄架下，等长辈先开口。

branches.en: a brother's son arriving with a suitcase
branches.cn: 提着行李箱到来的哥哥的儿子

branches.en: a sister's son helping in the kitchen
branches.cn: 在厨房帮忙的姐姐的儿子

branches.en: a wedding table shared by both families
branches.cn: 两家人共用的一张婚宴桌

branches.en: a partner's nephew calling at the door
branches.cn: 伴侣的侄子来敲门

branches.en: an old chronicle naming an heir
branches.cn: 旧编年史里指定继承人的那一页

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin noun of kinship, its feminine partner, the French form that narrowed it, and the English words built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语亲属名词、它的阴性对应词、把它收窄的法语形式，以及同一词干上的英语词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied nepos for the male kinsman and neptis for the female counterpart, and French carried the narrowed nephew into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了男性亲属词 nepos 与阴性对应词 neptis，法语把收窄后的 nephew 带入英语。

definition_zh: 此外；而且；再者
definition_en: in addition to what has just been said, used to add another point
core_image: 一段论证之后又添上一个更有力的理由
scene: 这个方案便宜；此外，它还很安全。 The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is safe.
sceneCN: 这里 furthermore 是「此外」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个方案便宜；此外，它还很安全。

senses.title: Adding a point
senses.definition: used to introduce another point that supports what was said
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出另一个支持前文的论点
senses.example: The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is safe.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案便宜；此外，它还很安全。
senses.why: This is the main linking sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的连接义项。

senses.title: Building an argument
senses.definition: used to strengthen an argument by adding a reason
senses.definitionCN: 通过补充理由来加强论证
senses.example: The room was small; furthermore, it was dark.
senses.exampleCN: 房间很小；而且，它还很暗。
senses.why: The added point pushes the argument forward.
senses.whyCN: 补充的论点把论证向前推进。

senses.title: Formal emphasis
senses.definition: used in formal writing to add emphasis to a further point
senses.definitionCN: 在正式写作中用来强调进一步的论点
senses.example: She was tired; furthermore, she had no money.
senses.exampleCN: 她累了；再者，她也没有钱。
senses.why: The word often marks a formal list of reasons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常标志正式的理由罗列。

intro.en: Furthermore is a compound of further and more, both old English words.
intro.cn: furthermore 由古英语词 further 和 more 复合而成。

items.en: Furthur meant further or more distant.
items.cn: furthur 意为更远或更向前。

items.en: Further grew to mean additional.
items.cn: further 逐渐表示额外的。

items.en: More was joined to form furthermore.
items.cn: more 被加上去，形成 furthermore。

items.en: It became a formal linking adverb.
items.cn: 它成为正式的连接副词。

items.en: Writers use it to stack reasons.
items.cn: 写作者用它来层层叠加理由。

note.en: Furthermore is compared with look-alike words and other linking adverbs.
note.cn: 把 furthermore 与形近词以及其他连接副词作比较。

entries.definition: to a greater degree
at a greater distance
most important
in addition to that
in addition
as an extra thing

normalIntro.en: Furthermore adds one more reason to what you have said.
normalIntro.cn: furthermore 在说过的话上再加一条理由。

normal.en: The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is safe.
normal.cn: 这个方案便宜；此外，它还很安全。

normal.en: The room was small; furthermore, it was dark.
normal.cn: 房间很小；而且，它还很暗。

normal.en: She was tired; furthermore, she had no money.
normal.cn: 她累了；再者，她也没有钱。

normal.en: Furthermore, the report offers no proof.
normal.cn: 此外，这份报告没有提供证据。

normal.en: The road is long; furthermore, it is steep.
normal.cn: 路很长；而且，还很陡。

abstract.en: A list grows stronger when each reason supports the last.
abstract.cn: 当每个理由都支撑前一个时，清单会更有力。

abstract.en: Further and more are two steps in one direction.
abstract.cn: further 和 more 是同一方向上的两步。

abstract.en: Good arguments are built, not shouted.
abstract.cn: 好的论证是搭建出来的，不是喊出来的。

examples.en: The plan is cheap; furthermore, it is safe.
examples.cn: 这个方案便宜；此外，它还很安全。

examples.en: The room was small; furthermore, it was dark.
examples.cn: 房间很小；而且，它还很暗。

examples.en: She was tired; furthermore, she had no money.
examples.cn: 她累了；再者，她也没有钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: furthermore 等于 further 加 more；与 moreover 意思相近，常用于正式写作。

root: 由 further（更向前）加 more（更多）复合而成，核心义「在已有的基础上再添一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Furthermore is a formal adverb that adds another supporting point.
sensesIntro.cn: furthermore 是正式副词，用来补充另一个支持性论点。

core.en: One more step added to what is already said.
core.cn: 在已说内容上再添一步。

branches.en: A new point joins the list.
branches.cn: 新的论点加入清单。

branches.en: The added reason supports the claim.
branches.cn: 补充的理由支持主张。

branches.en: Formal writing stacks reasons neatly.
branches.cn: 正式写作把理由整齐叠放。

branches.en: Addition and support work together.
branches.cn: 添加与支撑共同起作用。

branches.en: The same link serves speech and essay.
branches.cn: 同一个连接词服务于口语和文章。

intro.en: Furthermore belongs to a family built on further.
intro.cn: furthermore 属于以 further 为核心的一组词。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都是本族英语词，而非拉丁语。

items.meaning: at a greater distance or degree
items.exampleCN: 我们需要进一步的证据。
最远的那座房子是空的。

items.example: The gift was given in furtherance of the project.
items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是为了推进这个项目。

items.example: Her work is furthering the research.
items.exampleCN: 她的工作正在推进这项研究。

items.example: He returned to further education at forty.
items.exampleCN: 他四十岁重返继续教育。

items.example: They looked further afield for a house.
The furthermost island has no people.

definition_zh: 合作的；协作的；共同完成的
definition_en: involving two or more people or groups that work together on a shared task
core_image: 几个人围着同一张桌子，把各自的笔迹写到一页纸上
scene: 项目组每周碰头，把各自负责的部分拼到一起。 The team took a collaborative approach to the design.
sceneCN: 这里 collaborative 指「协作的」（第 1 个义项：多方共同参与的）；句意是团队在设计上采取了协作的方式。

pos.zh: 合作的；协作的；共同完成的

senses.title: Working together on a task
senses.definition: involving people or groups that work together on one shared task
senses.definitionCN: 由多方共同完成同一任务的
senses.example: The two schools ran a collaborative art show.
senses.exampleCN: 两所学校合办了一场艺术展。
senses.why: The Latin base meant working, and the prefix added the idea of together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为工作，前缀又加上了一起的含义。

senses.title: Designed for joint use
senses.definition: made so that several people can work on it at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 设计成可供多人同时使用的
senses.example: They opened a collaborative editing tool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开放了一个协同编辑工具。
senses.why: Software extended the word from people to shared workspaces.
senses.whyCN: 软件把这个词从人扩展到共享的工作空间。

intro.en: Collaborative goes back to Latin laborare, to work, with the prefix com-, together.
intro.cn: collaborative 上溯拉丁语 laborare（工作），前缀 com- 表示一起。

items.en: Laborare meant to work or to toil.
items.cn: laborare 意为工作或劳作。

items.en: Collaborare joined com- with laborare to mean work together.
items.cn: collaborare 把 com- 与 laborare 结合，意为一起工作。

items.en: French collaboration named joint work, often in science.
items.cn: 法语 collaboration 指共同工作，常用于科学。

items.en: English adopted collaborate and soon formed collaborative.
items.cn: 英语先吸收 collaborate，很快又造出 collaborative。

items.en: The word now covers shared software and shared classrooms.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖共享软件与共享课堂。

note.en: The look-alike group holds adjectives and nouns built on similar Latin shapes, while the meaning group names what is shared and done together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是由相似拉丁形式构成的形容词与名词，近义组列出共同与共享。

entries.definition: willing to help and work with other people
entries.definitionCN: 愿意帮助他人并与他人合作的

entries.definition: relating to a large company
a person who works with another on a task
entries.definitionCN: 与他人共同完成一项任务的人

entries.definition: shared by two or more people or groups
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同拥有的

entries.definition: done by a group acting as a whole
entries.definitionCN: 由整体群体共同完成的

entries.definition: used or owned by more than one person
entries.definitionCN: 由不止一人使用或拥有的

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from the Latin root for work and the prefix for together.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从拉丁语的工作词根与表示一起的前缀搭起这个词。

normal.en: Find labor inside the word: collaborative work is shared labour.
normal.cn: 词里藏着 labor：协作的工作就是分担的劳动。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, as in company and community.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，company 与 community 也是如此。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes it an adjective, a quality of a group.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 使它成为形容词，表示群体的一种性质。

normal.en: Collaborate is the verb, collaboration the noun, collaborative the adjective.
normal.cn: collaborate 是动词，collaboration 是名词，collaborative 是形容词。

normal.en: A collaborative tool lets several hands work on one page.
normal.cn: 协作工具让好几只手同时改同一页。

abstract.en: Picture four chairs pulled up to one wide table.
abstract.cn: 想象四把椅子围到一张宽桌旁。

abstract.en: Picture two hands holding the same pen above a map.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在同一张地图上方共握一支笔。

abstract.en: Picture a screen where three cursors move at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕上同时移动着三个光标。

examples.en: The report was a collaborative effort by three departments.
examples.cn: 这份报告是三个部门共同努力的成果。

examples.en: Students learn faster in a collaborative classroom.
examples.cn: 学生在协作式的课堂里学得更快。

examples.en: The app offers collaborative notes for small teams.
examples.cn: 这款应用为小团队提供协作笔记。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collaborative 记成 com 加 labor：几个人一起干活，就是协作。

root: 源自拉丁语 laborare（工作）加前缀 com-（一起），经法语进入英语，指多方共同参与。

sensesIntro.en: From people sharing a task to tools that let many hands work on one page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共同承担一项任务的人，到让多只手同改一页的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several people bent over one table, adding to the same page.
core.cn: 核心意象：几个人俯身同一张桌子，往同一页上添写。

branches.en: The human sense is the oldest: people working on one task.
branches.cn: 人的义项最古老：人们共同做一件事。

branches.en: The tool sense transfers the idea to shared software.
branches.cn: 工具义项把这个想法转移到共享软件上。

branches.en: Both senses depend on more than one participant.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖不止一个参与者。

branches.en: Shared labour is the literal meaning hidden in the Latin root.
branches.cn: 分担的劳动正是藏在拉丁词根里的字面义。

branches.en: A collaborative tool is only useful when others join in.
branches.cn: 协作工具只有在别人加入时才发挥作用。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin root labor, with com- for together and -ive for the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词族建在拉丁词根 labor 上，com- 表一起，-ive 构成形容词。

latinIntro.en: Laborare, to work, is the living Latin base behind collaborate and laboratory.
latinIntro.cn: laborare（工作）是 collaborate 与 laboratory 背后活的拉丁词基。

items.example: The two labs collaborate on the vaccine.
items.exampleCN: 这两个实验室合作研发疫苗。

items.example: The book grew out of a long collaboration.
items.exampleCN: 这本书源于一次长期合作。

items.meaning: a person who works with another
items.exampleCN: 她的主要合作者住在国外。

items.meaning: in a way that involves working together
items.example: The students wrote the chapter collaboratively.
items.exampleCN: 学生们合作写成了这一章。

items.meaning: hard work or to work hard
items.example: The project took years of labor.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目花了数年的辛劳。

items.example: Copying the files by hand was laborious.
items.exampleCN: 手工抄写这些文件很费力。

items.meaning: to add details or to be very detailed
items.example: He refused to elaborate on the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他拒绝进一步说明这个计划。

items.meaning: a room used for scientific work
items.example: The samples were sent to the laboratory.

latinEntries.example: Latin collaborare joins com- with laborare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collaborare 由 com- 与 laborare 组合而成。

latinEntries.meaning: to work, toil or suffer effort
latinEntries.example: Laborare is the source of labour and laboratory.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laborare 是 labour 与 laboratory 的来源。

definition_zh: 方便；便利设施；方便的时候
definition_en: the quality of being easy to use or reach, something that makes life easier, or a time that suits someone
core_image: 门边一排按钮，伸手就能按到
scene: 楼下小店延长了营业时间，加晚班的人顺路就能买东西。 The shop opens late for the convenience of workers.
sceneCN: 这里 convenience 指「方便」（第 1 个义项：与人的需要相合而省力）；句意是这家店为方便工人而开到很晚。

pos.zh: 方便；便利设施；方便的时候

senses.title: Ease of use
senses.definition: the quality of fitting easily with a person's needs
senses.definitionCN: 与人的需要相合而省力的性质
senses.example: The app was chosen for its convenience.
senses.exampleCN: 选这个应用是因为它方便。
senses.why: Anything that saves a step feels like a small gift.
senses.whyCN: 能省一步的东西，都像一份小礼物。

senses.title: A helpful facility
senses.definition: a device or service that makes daily life easier
senses.definitionCN: 让日常生活更省力的设备或服务
senses.example: The flat has every modern convenience.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓有各种现代便利设施。
senses.why: Comfort is often a row of small machines.
senses.whyCN: 舒适常常是一排小小的机器。

senses.title: A suitable moment
senses.definition: a time that suits a person well
senses.definitionCN: 适合某人安排的时间
senses.example: Please reply at your convenience.
senses.exampleCN: 请在您方便时回复。
senses.why: The word also hands a person their own clock.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也把时间的表盘交还给对方。

intro.en: Convenience comes from Latin convenientia, a coming together, from convenire, to come together, built on com-, together, and venire, to come.
intro.cn: convenience 来自拉丁语 convenientia（相合），源于 convenire（走到一起），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

items.en: Venire meant to come or to arrive.
items.cn: venire 意为来或到达。

items.en: Convenire meant to come together in one place.
items.cn: convenire 意为来到同一个地方。

items.en: Convenientia named the fitting together of two things.
items.cn: convenientia 指两件事彼此相合。

items.en: French convenance kept the sense of fitting well.
items.cn: 法语 convenance 保留了恰好相合之义。

items.en: English convenience meant suitableness and ease.
items.cn: 英语 convenience 指适宜与省力。

items.en: It also names the machines and services that save effort.
items.cn: 它也指省力的机器与服务。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin coming base ven-, and the meaning group names other words for ease and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的来词基 ven-，近义组列出其他表示省力与舒适的词。

entries.definition: easy to use or reach
in an easy or suitable way
trouble caused by something
the absence of difficulty or effort
a pleasant state of ease
a place or service built for a purpose

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a step saved, then move to a row of small machines and to a time handed back to you.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从省下的一步开始，再到一排小机器，最后到交还给你的一段时间。

normal.en: Con- is together and ven is come, so convenience is things coming together nicely.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，ven 是来，convenience 就是万物恰好凑到一起。

normal.en: A button within reach is convenience made visible.
normal.cn: 伸手可及的按钮，就是看得见的方便。

normal.en: Every machine that saves a step joins the word.
normal.cn: 每一件省一步的机器，都加入了这个词。

normal.en: At your convenience means you hold the clock.
normal.cn: at your convenience 的意思是钟表由你拿着。

normal.en: Less effort is the whole idea.
normal.cn: 少花力气，就是全部的意思。

abstract.en: Picture one hand reaching a switch without standing up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手不用起身就够到开关。

abstract.en: Picture a row of machines blinking in a small flat.
abstract.cn: 想象小公寓里一排机器闪着灯。

abstract.en: Picture a door left unlocked at a late hour.
abstract.cn: 想象很晚的时候一扇没锁的门。

examples.en: The hotel is chosen for its convenience.
examples.cn: 选这家酒店是因为它方便。

examples.en: Reply at your convenience, there is no hurry.
examples.cn: 你方便时回复即可，不急。

examples.en: The village now has many modern conveniences.
examples.cn: 这个村子如今有许多现代便利设施。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convenience 记成 con（一起）加 ven（来）加 ience：需要的东西恰好在身边凑齐，就是方便。

root: 源自拉丁语 convenientia（相合），来自 convenire（走到一起），由 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成，指省力、便利设施与合适的时机。

sensesIntro.en: From effort saved, to the tools that save it, and at last to the hour you choose yourself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从省下的力气，到替你省力的工具，最后到由你自己挑选的时辰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching a switch without standing up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手不用起身就够到开关。

branches.en: The core sense is simply effort taken away.
branches.cn: 核心义项就是拿走了一部分力气。

branches.en: The machines that take it away get the same name.
branches.cn: 拿走力气的机器也得到了同一个名字。

branches.en: Even a good hour can be called convenient.
branches.cn: 连一个好时辰也能被称为方便。

branches.en: Ease and the tools of ease belong together.
branches.cn: 省力与省力的工具本就在一起。

branches.en: A service saves time, and a free hour receives it.
branches.cn: 服务省下时间，空闲的钟点接住它。

intro.en: Convenience is built on Latin com-, together, plus venire, to come.
intro.cn: convenience 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 venire（来）构成。

latinIntro.en: The coming base ven- also appears in convene, convention and event.
latinIntro.cn: 来词基 ven- 也出现在 convene、convention 与 event 中。

items.meaning: a state of things fitting together
items.example: The shop is open for convenience.
items.exampleCN: 这家店为方便顾客而开着。

items.meaning: in a fitting or easy way
items.exampleCN: 公交站就在附近很方便。
我们为这带来的不便致歉。

items.meaning: to call people to come together
a coming together or an agreed habit
items.meaningCN: 聚到一起或共同接受的惯例

definition_zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状的小圆物
definition_en: a round green seed that grows in a long pod and is eaten as a vegetable; also a small round object that looks like this seed
core_image: 拇指沿着豆荚的缝一压，一排圆豆滚进掌心
scene: 菜园里藤蔓顺着竹架往上爬，几个鼓鼓的豆荚垂在叶子下面。 He split a pod open and the small green peas rolled across the cutting board.
sceneCN: 这里是「豌豆」（第 1 个义项：长在豆荚里的绿色圆粒）；句意是他掰开一个豆荚，小小的绿豌豆滚到了砧板上。画面里有竹架、豆荚与砧板。

pos.zh: 豌豆；豌豆粒；豌豆状小圆物

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 pisum 经古英语 pise 演变而来的旧式集体名词，后来被复数 peas 取代，义为「豌豆（总称）」
由 pea 与 sized 复合而成，义为「豌豆大小的」
由 pea 与 soup 复合而成，指用豌豆煮成的浓汤

senses.title: A round green seed grown in a pod
senses.definition: a climbing plant of the legume family, or the round green seed it bears inside a long pod
senses.definitionCN: 豆科的一种攀缘植物，或它结在长豆荚里的绿色圆粒种子
senses.example: Peas need a trellis to climb in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 在小菜园里，豌豆需要有个架子才能往上爬。
senses.why: Latin pisum named both the plant and its seed, so the word begins as the name of a crop rather than of a single grain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pisum 兼指这种植物与它的种子，所以这个词最初是作物的名字，而不是单独一粒豆的名字。

senses.title: The seed eaten as a vegetable
senses.definition: the seed harvested while still green and soft, cooked as a vegetable or sold frozen and canned
senses.definitionCN: 在仍青嫩时采收的种子，作为蔬菜烹调，或以冷冻、罐装形式出售
senses.example: She added a cup of frozen peas to the rice.
senses.exampleCN: 她往米饭里加了一杯冷冻豌豆。
senses.why: Once the crop reaches the kitchen, the same word names the food on the plate, and the plural is the usual form because peas are eaten in numbers.
senses.whyCN: 当这种作物进了厨房，同一个词就指盘中的食物；因为豌豆总是成把地吃，复数形式反而更常用。

senses.title: A small round object like a pea
senses.definition: any small round thing that resembles a pea in size or shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何在大小或形状上像豌豆的小圆物
senses.example: The beads were the size of peas and just as smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 那些珠子有豌豆大小，也一样光滑。
senses.why: A pea is a ready-made standard of smallness and roundness, so English borrows the vegetable to describe beads, pellets and other tiny spheres.
senses.whyCN: 豌豆是现成的「小而圆」的标准，于是英语借这种蔬菜来描述珠子、小丸等微小的球状物。

intro.en: Pea comes from a Latin name for the pulse, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: pea 来自拉丁语对这种豆类的称呼，经古英语形式传入，后来又被英语截短成现在的样子。

items.en: Pisum was the Latin name for the pea plant and its seed, and it stands behind most European names for the vegetable.
items.cn: pisum 是拉丁语中对豌豆植株及其种子的称呼，也是欧洲多数语言里这个蔬菜名称的来源。

items.en: Greek pison named the same pulse and is generally thought to come from an older Mediterranean language rather than from Greek itself.
items.cn: 希腊语 pison 指同一种豆类，一般认为它来自更早的地中海语言，而不是希腊语本身。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word as pise or pyse, a singular form that also served as a mass noun for the crop.
items.cn: 古英语借入后写作 pise 或 pyse，这个单数形式同时也当集体名词，指这种作物。

items.en: Middle English used pease for one seed and for many, so speakers began to hear the ending as a plural marker.
items.cn: 中古英语用 pease 兼指一粒和许多粒，于是人们开始把这个词尾听成复数标记。

items.en: English cut the word back to pea as a new singular and formed peas as its plural, a process known as back-formation.
items.cn: 英语把词截短成 pea 作为新的单数，再造出复数 peas，这种过程称为逆构词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the old form of the word, a close compound and two words that merely share its sound; the near-meaning group collects other edible seeds.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的旧形式、一个近亲复合词，以及两个只是读音相近的词；近义组收其他可食用的种子。

entries.definition: The older form of the word, now archaic or dialectal, kept alive in pease pudding.
entries.definitionCN: 这个词的旧形式，现已古旧或限于方言，保留在豌豆泥这一说法里。

entries.definition: The seed of a low plant in the same family, named by joining pea and nut.
entries.definitionCN: 同科矮生植物结的种子，由 pea 与 nut 拼合命名。

entries.definition: A hard round gem formed inside an oyster; only the spelling is close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 牡蛎体内形成的坚硬圆珠；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The pointed top of a mountain; only the sound and spelling are close, the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 山峰的尖顶；只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An edible seed of a climbing plant, often kidney-shaped.
entries.definitionCN: 攀缘植物结的可食用种子，常呈肾形。

entries.definition: A small flat seed of a plant in the same family, usually cooked in soup.
entries.definitionCN: 同科植物结的小扁种子，通常煮汤食用。

entries.definition: Any plant that bears pods, or the edible seed of such a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 任何结豆荚的植物，或这类植物的可食用种子。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin seed name that English shortened twice over, so its history is a lesson in how plurals can reshape a singular.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的种子名称，英语先后把它截短了两次，它的历史正好说明复数如何反过来重塑单数。

normal.en: Latin pisum is the oldest recorded name of the seed, and it survives almost unchanged in French pois and Italian pisello.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pisum 是这种种子最早的名称记录，在法语 pois 与意大利语 pisello 里几乎原样保留。

normal.en: English once said pease for one seed and for many, which is why peas now sounds like a plain plural of pea.
normal.cn: 英语曾用 pease 兼指一粒与许多粒，所以今天的 peas 听起来就是 pea 的普通复数。

normal.en: A pea is defined by its pod: the seeds grow in a row inside a long case that splits along one seam.
normal.cn: 豌豆由豆荚来定义：种子成排长在一个长壳里，壳沿着一条缝裂开。

normal.en: Pea green and pea-sized both take the vegetable as a standard of colour and of smallness.
normal.cn: pea green 与 pea-sized 都拿这种蔬菜当作颜色与大小的标准。

normal.en: The noun is countable now, so one says one pea, two peas, and a bowl of peas.
normal.cn: 这个名词现在是可数的，所以说一粒豌豆、两粒豌豆、一碗豌豆。

abstract.en: A pea is a seed that carries its own food and its own case, a small complete package.
abstract.cn: 豌豆是一粒自带养料、自带外壳的种子，一个小而完整的包裹。

abstract.en: The word shrank from pease to pea because speakers rebuilt a singular out of a plural they had misheard.
abstract.cn: 这个词从 pease 缩成 pea，是因为说话人把自己听错的复数重新造成了单数。

abstract.en: Anything small, round and green can be called pea-like, which shows how a vegetable becomes a unit of size.
abstract.cn: 凡是小而圆、颜色发绿的东西都能说成像豌豆，这显示一种蔬菜如何变成大小的单位。

examples.en: She shelled a bowl of peas for dinner.
examples.cn: 她剥了一碗豌豆准备做晚饭。

examples.en: The soup was thick with split peas and ham.
examples.cn: 汤里满是干豌豆和火腿，十分浓稠。

examples.en: Each bead was the size of a pea and smooth as glass.
examples.cn: 每颗珠子都有豌豆大小，光滑得像玻璃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮」——剥开豆荚那层皮，里面就是豌豆；pea 就是豌豆。

root: 来自拉丁语 pisum（豌豆），经古英语 pise、中古英语 pease 演变，近代英语逆构出单数 pea；与表示和平的 peace 只是同音，来源完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seed inside the pod; the senses move from the growing crop to the food on the plate and then to any tiny round thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是豆荚里的种子；义项从地里的作物，移到盘中的食物，再移到任何微小的圆物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thumb pressing the seam of a pod until a row of round seeds rolls into the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：拇指压开豆荚的缝，一排圆豆滚进掌心。

branches.en: a vine climbing a bamboo frame in a kitchen garden
branches.cn: 菜园里顺着竹架往上爬的藤

branches.en: a pod splitting open above a dinner plate
branches.cn: 餐盘上方裂开的豆荚

branches.en: a cup of frozen peas tipped into boiling rice
branches.cn: 一杯冻豌豆倒进沸着的米饭

branches.en: beads rolling across a table, each the size of a seed
branches.cn: 滚过桌面的珠子，颗颗如豆

branches.en: a seed used as a measure for anything very small
branches.cn: 拿豆粒来衡量极细小之物的做法

intro.en: The word comes down from a Latin name for the seed, filtered through an Old English form that English later cut in two.
intro.cn: 这个词源自拉丁语中表示种子的名称，经古英语形式过滤，后来又被英语截成两段。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

pea, used for one or for many
a dish of boiled split peas

definition_zh: 惊吓；使害怕；受惊
definition_en: to make someone feel afraid, or to become afraid
core_image: 半夜一声怪响，孩子们猛地缩进被子里
scene: 半夜的怪声把孩子们吓坏了。 A strange noise scared the children at midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 scare 是「惊吓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：半夜的怪声吓坏了孩子们。

senses.title: Frighten someone
senses.definition: to make a person or animal feel afraid
senses.definitionCN: 使人或动物感到害怕
senses.example: The loud bang scared the dog.
senses.exampleCN: 巨响吓到了狗。
senses.why: The core sense is causing sudden fear.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是引起突然的恐惧。

senses.title: Become frightened
senses.definition: to become afraid, especially of a sudden danger
senses.definitionCN: 尤指面对突然危险时变得害怕
senses.example: The horse scares easily at loud sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹马容易被大声响吓到。
senses.why: The same action can be felt from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作也可以从受惊者内部来感受。

senses.title: Sudden alarm
senses.definition: a sudden feeling or period of public fear
senses.definitionCN: 突然的恐惧感或公众恐慌期
senses.example: The food scare led to empty shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 食品恐慌导致货架空荡。
senses.why: The verb becomes the name of the fear it creates.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为它所造成的恐惧的名称。

intro.en: Scare comes from Old Norse skjarr, timid, and entered English in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: scare 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），于中世纪进入英语。

items.en: Skjarr meant timid or easily frightened.
items.cn: skjarr 意为胆怯的、易受惊的。

items.en: Skerren meant to frighten or drive away.
items.cn: skerren 意为使害怕或驱赶。

items.en: Scare became the common verb for sudden fear.
items.cn: scare 成为表示突然恐惧的常用动词。

items.en: Scarecrow and scare tactics entered common use.
items.cn: scarecrow 与 scare tactics 进入常用语。

items.en: Scare also names public alarms such as health scares.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scare 也指健康恐慌等公众警报。

note.en: Scare is compared with similar spellings and with other fear verbs.
note.cn: 把 scare 与形近词以及其它表示恐惧的动词作比较。

entries.definition: a mark left by a wound
a cloth worn around the neck
not enough
to make someone afraid
to make someone worried or afraid
to frighten someone very much

normalIntro.en: Scare is one letter away from scar, and both come from harm.
normalIntro.cn: scare 与 scar 只差一个字母，都与伤害有关。

normal.en: A scare can leave a scar on the memory.
normal.cn: 一次惊吓可能在记忆里留下疤痕。

normal.en: Scared is the adjective for feeling fear.
normal.cn: scared 是表示感到害怕的形容词。

normal.en: A scarecrow scares birds away from crops.
normal.cn: 稻草人把鸟从庄稼旁吓走。

normal.en: Scare away and scare off both mean drive off.
normal.cn: scare away 与 scare off 都表示吓退。

normal.en: A health scare is a sudden public worry about illness.
normal.cn: health scare 是关于疾病的突然公众担忧。

abstract.en: Fear arrives in a second but can last for years.
abstract.cn: 恐惧一秒钟到来，却可能持续多年。

abstract.en: A scare tests whether we can still think clearly.
abstract.cn: 惊吓检验我们是否还能清醒思考。

abstract.en: The same word names the act and the alarm.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指吓人的动作，也指惊慌。

examples.en: Don't scare me like that again.
examples.cn: 别再那样吓我了。

examples.en: The dog scared the birds out of the garden.
examples.cn: 狗把鸟吓出了花园。

examples.en: The city recovered after the food scare.
examples.cn: 食品恐慌过后，城市恢复了平静。

dict_mnemonic.text: scare 与 scar 形近，可记「被吓（scare）得留下疤（scar）」，核心是突然使人害怕。

root: 源自古诺尔斯语 skjarr（胆怯的），经中古英语 skerren 进入英语，核心义「使人突然害怕」。

sensesIntro.en: Scare means to frighten someone, to become frightened, or a sudden alarm.
sensesIntro.cn: scare 意为吓唬某人、受惊害怕，或突然的恐慌。

core.en: Sudden fear caused by a threat.
core.cn: 由威胁引起的突然恐惧。

branches.en: Causing fear in another person or animal.
branches.cn: 使他人或动物产生恐惧。

branches.en: Being startled and feeling afraid.
branches.cn: 受到惊吓并感到害怕。

branches.en: A period of fear shared by many people.
branches.cn: 许多人共同经历的恐慌期。

branches.en: The giver and receiver of fear share one verb.
branches.cn: 施加恐惧者与承受恐惧者共用一个动词。

branches.en: A threat can scare one person or a whole city.
branches.cn: 一个威胁可以吓到一个人或整座城市。

intro.en: Scare builds a family of adjectives, tools, and tactics.
intro.cn: scare 构成形容词、工具和策略等词族。

latinIntro.en: Scare is Germanic, from Old Norse, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: scare 源自日耳曼语族中的古诺尔斯语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.meaning: to frighten or a sudden alarm

items.example: She was scared of the dark.

items.meaning: a person or thing that scares
items.example: The machine is a bird scarer.

items.meaning: a figure set up to frighten birds
items.example: A scarecrow stood in the field.

items.exampleCN: 这场运动使用了恐吓手段。

definition_zh: 重建；重振；重新组装
definition_en: to build again what was destroyed; to restore a system or feeling; to assemble something anew
core_image: 废墟上第一块新砖被稳稳放下
scene: 地震过后，工人在断裂的墙边重新砌起第一层砖。 Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
sceneCN: 这里 rebuild 是「重建」（第 1 个义项：重新建造被毁之物）；句意为施工队开始重建受损的学校。画面里可留意：废墟旁的新砖、断裂的墙。

senses.title: To build again what was destroyed
senses.definition: to construct again something that has been damaged or destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 重新建造被损坏或被毁的东西
senses.example: Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
senses.exampleCN: 施工队开始重建受损的学校。
senses.why: The prefix re- means again, and build is the old verb for raising a structure, so rebuild is literally to raise it a second time.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 re- 意为「再次」，build 是「建造」的古动词，因此 rebuild 字面就是「再造一次」。

senses.title: To restore a system or feeling
senses.definition: to bring back the strength of an economy, an organization, or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 恢复经济、组织或关系的力量
senses.example: The new coach helped rebuild the team's confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练帮助球队重建了信心。
senses.why: A structure and a relationship share the same frame, so building again became a metaphor for restoring strength.
senses.whyCN: 建筑与人际关系共用同一框架，于是「再建一次」成了「恢复力量」的隐喻。

senses.title: To put together anew
senses.definition: to assemble something again from its parts, often in a new form
senses.definitionCN: 把事物的各部分重新组装，常以新形态呈现
senses.example: Engineers had to rebuild the engine from spare parts.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师不得不用备用零件重新组装发动机。
senses.why: The prefix adds repetition rather than repair, so the word also covers taking something apart and assembling it again.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀带来的是重复而非修理，所以这个词也涵盖拆开再组装。

intro.en: Rebuild joins a Latin prefix of repetition to a native English verb of construction, and then extends the image from walls to people.
intro.cn: rebuild 把表重复的拉丁前缀与英语本族的「建造」动词结合，再把这一形象从墙延伸到人。

items.en: Byldan meant to build or to dwell, the native verb behind build.
items.cn: byldan 意为建造或居住，是 build 背后的本族动词。

items.en: The Latin prefix re- added the idea of again to the verb.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 为这个动词加上「再次」的意思。

items.en: Middle English rebuilden joined prefix and verb into a single word.
items.cn: 中古英语 rebuilden 把前缀与动词合成一个词。

items.en: Modern English extended rebuild from houses to systems, teams, and feelings.
items.cn: 现代英语把 rebuild 从房屋扩展到系统、团队与情感。

items.en: Rebuilding confidence borrows the image of a structure raised again.
items.cn: 重建信心借用了「结构再立一次」的形象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short verbs beginning with re-; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of restoring and assembling.
note.cn: 形近组收以 re- 开头的短动词；近义组收表恢复与组装的动词。

entries.definition: To bind a book again.
To speak sharply to someone.
To argue against a claim.
To build again in full.
To bring back a former state.
To repair and modernise a building.
To put parts together again.

normalIntro.en: The word is simply again plus build, and the picture of a second raising runs through every sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是「再次」加「建造」，而「再立一次」的画面贯穿所有义项。

normal.en: Re plus build: build it once more, and you have rebuilt it.
normal.cn: re 加 build：再建一次，就是 rebuild。

normal.en: Rebuilt is the past form, so the pattern is rebuild, rebuilt, rebuilt.
normal.cn: 过去式是 rebuilt，变化模式是 rebuild、rebuilt、rebuilt。

normal.en: Rebuild trust and rebuild a bridge use the same verb in two scales.
normal.cn: rebuild trust 与 rebuild a bridge 是同一个动词的两种尺度。

normal.en: From scratch is a common partner, meaning with nothing left to reuse.
normal.cn: from scratch 是常见搭配，意为没有可再利用的东西。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable, after the weak re-.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二音节，在轻读的 re- 之后。

abstract.en: What is rebuilt is not the old thing but a new thing in the old place.
abstract.cn: 重建的并不是旧物，而是在旧地点的新的东西。

abstract.en: Repair fixes a crack; rebuilding accepts that the crack cannot be fixed.
abstract.cn: 修理补一道缝，重建则承认那道缝已无法修补。

abstract.en: A person who rebuilds is betting that the future is worth the labour.
abstract.cn: 选择重建的人，是在赌未来值得这份劳作。

examples.en: Crews began to rebuild the damaged school.
examples.cn: 施工队开始重建受损的学校。

examples.en: The new coach helped rebuild the team's confidence.
examples.cn: 新教练帮助球队重建了信心。

examples.en: Engineers had to rebuild the engine from spare parts.
examples.cn: 工程师不得不用备用零件重新组装发动机。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 build（建造）：再建一次就是重建；把信心、经济再建起来，也是 rebuild。

root: 古英语 byldan（建造）+ 前缀 re-（再次）→ 中古英语 rebuilden → 现代英语 rebuild；同族有 rebuilt、rebuilding。

sensesIntro.en: The core is raising a structure a second time; the senses extend from buildings to systems and to assemblies.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把结构再立一次」；义项从建筑延伸到系统与组装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first new brick laid on a field of rubble.
core.cn: 核心意象：废墟上放下第一块新砖。

branches.en: a brick laid on rubble
branches.cn: 在废墟上放下一块砖

branches.en: a team finding its confidence
branches.cn: 球队重新找回信心

branches.en: an engine taken apart and refitted
branches.cn: 发动机被拆开再装回

branches.en: stone and spirit rebuilt
branches.cn: 砖石与精神一起重建

branches.en: a system and a machine reassembled
branches.cn: 系统与机器被重新组装

intro.en: A Latin prefix of repetition meets a native English building verb, which gives the word its simple shape.
intro.cn: 一个表重复的拉丁前缀遇上英语本族的建造动词，构成了这个词的简单外形。

latinIntro.en: The only Latin element is the prefix re-, meaning again or back; build itself is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 唯一的拉丁元素是前缀 re-，意为「再次、回」；build 本身是英语本族词。
